一.etymology: Pure ideograph (指事): a single horizontal stroke — one counting rod laid on the ground. The simplest possible written sign, unchanged since oracle-bone script.
一.mnemonic: One stroke, one finger laid flat, one horizon. Everything in the writing system is built on top of this line — it is the floor the other kanji stand on.

lesson_examples.jp: 一緒（いっしょ）に　行（い）かない？
lesson_examples.en: Do you want to come along?

lesson_examples.jp: 一休（ひとやす）み　しませんか。

右.etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand (𠂇) over a mouth (口) — the right hand, the one you eat with and raise to speak or swear.
右.mnemonic: The hand that carries food to the mouth: your right — みぎ. Stroke tip: the sweep goes first here, then the horizontal — mirror etiquette to 左.

lesson_examples.jp: 右腕（うわん）が　上（あ）がりません。
lesson_examples.en: I can't lift my right arm.

lesson_examples.jp: 右（みぎ）に　曲（ま）がってください。

雨.etymology: Pictograph: the vault of the sky as a canopy, with four drops falling inside it. As a crown component it governs all weather kanji (雪, 雲, 電).
雨.mnemonic: A window pane in a storm: four drops caught mid-fall behind the glass — あめ. When 雨 sits on a kanji's head, look up: weather incoming.

lesson_examples.jp: 雨（あめ）　降（ふ）っ　てる？
トムは　雨（あめ）　男（おとこ）だ。
lesson_examples.en: Every time Tom shows up, it rains.

円.etymology: Simplified from 圓: an enclosure (囗) around the phonetic 員. The perfect round shape — chosen in 1871 as the name of Japan's round coin: the yen.
円.mnemonic: A coin standing upright in its slot — まる, the circle; エン, the yen it became. Every price tag in Japan ends in this little window: 百円, 千円.

lesson_examples.jp: 80円（えん）　切手（きって）を　1枚（まい）　下（くだ）さい。
これは　円（えん）です。

下.etymology: Pure ideograph: a short mark placed under a base line — the mirror of 上. The pair appears together on the oldest oracle bones.
下.mnemonic: A root and a drop hanging under the ground line: down, below — した. Flip 上 in a mirror along the ground and it falls to become 下.

lesson_examples.jp: 許（ゆる）して下（くだ）さい。
連絡（れんらく）　して下（くだ）さい。

火.etymology: Pictograph: a flame rising from a burning pile, sparks flying off both sides. As a bottom component it flattens into four dots (灬).
火.mnemonic: A campfire: the central blaze and two sparks leaping away — ひ. Tuesday, 火曜日, is fire's day. Keep it away from 木 unless you want ashes.

lesson_examples.jp: 火（ひ）は　あついです。
まいにち　下火（したび）になる。

花.etymology: Phono-semantic: the grass crown (艹) gives the meaning — a plant — while 化 'change, transform' lends the reading カ. The plant transformed into its loveliest state: a flower.
花.mnemonic: Under the grass crown, a plant works its transformation (化) — and blooms: はな. 花見 is the festival of watching that magic happen.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　何（なに）という　花（はな）ですか？
これは　花嫁（はなよめ）です。

学.etymology: Simplified from 學: a child (子) under a roof, with hands above passing knowledge down. The three little strokes on top are all that remain of those hands.
学.mnemonic: A child under a sparkling roof — sparks of knowledge raining down from the teacher's hands: to study, まなぶ. 学校 is where the sparks fly, ガッコウ.

lesson_examples.jp: 大学生（だいがくせい）です。
学校（がっこう）は　どうですか？

気.etymology: Simplified from 氣: vapor (气) rising from cooking rice (米) — steam, breath, and by extension the invisible energy of weather and mood.
気.mnemonic: Steam curling off a pot of rice: invisible, but it moves everything — き. The sky's steam is 天気, yours is 元気. When both are good, life is too.

lesson_examples.jp: 元気（げんき）　出（だ）して。
元気（げんき）　出（だ）しなよ。

休.etymology: Compound ideograph: a person (亻) leaning against a tree (木) — resting in its shade. One of the textbook examples of a meaning built from two pictures.
休.mnemonic: A hiker slumped against a tree trunk, hat over the eyes — やすむ. 休み is that tree-shade taken as a day off.

lesson_examples.jp: 冬休（ふゆやす）み　何日（なんにち）から？
lesson_examples.en: When does your winter vacation begin?

lesson_examples.jp: ゆっくり　休（やす）んでね。

金.etymology: By the classic account: nuggets (the two dots) buried in layered earth (土) under a cover (𠆢) — metal in the mine. Later 'metal' in general, then gold and money.
金.mnemonic: Under a little roof, in the earth, two nuggets gleam — かね, gold, money. Friday, 金曜日, is payday: the day the nuggets reach your pocket.

lesson_examples.jp: お金（かね）は　どこ？
お金（かね）を　盗（ぬす）まれました。

九.etymology: Originally a pictograph of a bent elbow with a hand reaching in — borrowed for the number nine since oracle-bone times.
九.mnemonic: A baseball pitcher's arm frozen mid-throw, elbow bent, wrist hooked: nine innings, きゅう. The hook at the end is the ball leaving the hand.

lesson_examples.jp: 九（ここの）つの　いしを　ならべます。
これは　九（きゅう）です。

空.etymology: Phono-semantic: hole (穴) + 工 (phonetic クウ) — a hollowed-out space: empty; and the greatest hollow of all, the open sky.
空.mnemonic: Dig through the cave roof (穴) with your tools (工) and break into the biggest empty room there is: the sky — そら. 空港: the harbor of the sky.

lesson_examples.jp: 今週末（こんしゅうまつ）　空（あ）い　てる？
お　風呂（ふろ）　空（あ）い　てるよ。

月.etymology: Pictograph: the crescent moon with two shading strokes inside. One full cycle of the moon = one month.
月.mnemonic: The sun's window (日) grew legs and slimmed down for the night shift: the moon. It waxes and wanes once a month — つき / ゲツ, as in 月曜日, the moon's own day.

lesson_examples.jp: 娘（むすめ）が　6　月（つき）に　結婚（けっこん）　します。
lesson_examples.en: My daughter is getting married in June.

lesson_examples.jp: 娘（むすめ）は　6　月（つき）に　結婚（けっこん）　します。
lesson_examples.en: My daughter is getting married in June.

見.etymology: Compound ideograph: an eye (目) set on human legs (儿) — a person shown as nothing but their looking. To see is to walk your eye over to something.
見.mnemonic: An eyeball that grew legs and runs around looking at things — みる. When you 'go see' a friend, this little creature is what you send ahead.

lesson_examples.jp: それ　見（み）せて。
何（なに）　見（み）　てるの？

五.etymology: Ideograph: originally an X between two horizontal lines — a tally device marking the halfway point of ten. The X 'crosses over' at five.
五.mnemonic: The tally-keeper's shortcut: when you reach five, you stop drawing sticks and cross them off — ご! Four strokes that mean one full hand of fingers.

lesson_examples.jp: 五（いつ）つの　たまごを　かいます。
これは　五（ご）です。

口.etymology: Pictograph (象形): an open mouth, squared off by the brush. One of the most productive components in the writing system — anything spoken, eaten or shouted tends to contain it.
口.mnemonic: A wide-open mouth turned into a square frame. Every time you spot this box in a kanji, someone is talking, eating or shouting — くち.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　口（くち）が　堅（かた）い。
出口（でぐち）は　どこですか？

校.etymology: Phono-semantic: tree/wood (木) + 交 'to cross' (phonetic コウ). Originally wooden frames and fetters; settled on the wooden halls where paths cross — the school.
校.mnemonic: A wooden building (木) where a thousand lives crisscross (交) every morning — コウ, the school of 学校. Also the place your test gets 'crossed' with red ink.

lesson_examples.jp: 学校（がっこう）は　どうですか？
母（はは）は　高校（こうこう）の　先生（せんせい）です。
lesson_examples.en: My mother is a high school teacher.

左.etymology: Compound ideograph: a left hand (𠂇) holding a carpenter's tool (工). The left hand steadies the work while the right one acts.
左.mnemonic: The hand that holds the ruler (工) while the other draws: your left — ひだり. Stroke tip: here the horizontal goes first, then the sweep — the mirror of 右.

lesson_examples.jp: 左（ひだり）の　みちを　いきます。
lesson_examples.en: I take the road on the left.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　左利（ひだりき）きです。

三.etymology: Ideograph: three counting rods. Heaven, humankind and earth in the old Chinese reading of the three lines — top, middle, bottom.
三.mnemonic: Three floors of a building seen from the side. The middle floor is the smallest — the child between two parents.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　三塁打（さんるいだ）を　打（う）った。
トムは　三分（さんふん）　早（はや）く　ついた。

山.etymology: Pictograph: three peaks, the middle one highest. Unchanged in three thousand years.
山.mnemonic: Three peaks on the horizon — やま. Japan's favorite kanji: it caps 富士山 and half the family names in the country (山田, 山本).

lesson_examples.jp: 明日（あした）は　山登（やまのぼ）りに　行（い）ってきます。
lesson_examples.en: I'm going to go mountain climbing tomorrow.

lesson_examples.jp: 富士山（ふじさん）に　登（のぼ）った　ことは　ありますか？
lesson_examples.en: Have you ever climbed Mt. Fuji?

四.etymology: Originally written as four stacked bars (亖); the current form — breath dispersing from a mouth, drawn as legs inside a box — was borrowed for its sound over 2,000 years ago.
四.mnemonic: A window (the box) with a pair of legs dangling out of it: four legs in all if you count the window's own two sides. よん — the yawn of someone climbing out of that window.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　四（よっ）つです。
これは　四季（しき）です。

子.etymology: Pictograph: a swaddled baby — big head, arms spread wide, legs bound together in the wrapping cloth.
子.mnemonic: A baby with arms flung out and its legs still wrapped in a blanket — こ. Girls' names end with it (花子), and it hides in 好き: a woman with her child, fondness itself.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　賢（かしこ）い　子（こ）だ。
帽子（ぼうし）を　脱（ぬ）いで下（くだ）さい。

耳.etymology: Pictograph: an ear with its outer rim and lobe — the horizontal strokes trace the folds of the ear itself.
耳.mnemonic: An ear drawn in profile, lobe trailing off at the bottom stroke — みみ. Two of them frame your face; two strokes frame this kanji.

lesson_examples.jp: その　言葉（ことば）は　初耳（はつみみ）です。
lesson_examples.en: This is the first time I've heard that word.

lesson_examples.jp: ウサギは　どうして　耳（みみ）が　長（なが）い　んですか？
lesson_examples.en: Why do rabbits have long ears?

七.etymology: Originally a picture of a line being cut crosswise — it was the first way of writing 切 'to cut'. Borrowed early on for the number seven.
七.mnemonic: An upside-down seven with a hook. A knife slicing diagonally through a line: cut a cake into seven pieces — しち slices.

lesson_examples.jp: 七（なな）つの　ほしが　みえます。
これは　七（しち）です。

車.etymology: Pictograph: a cart seen from above — the axle running vertically, the wheel-body in the middle, crossbars at each end.
車.mnemonic: Bird's-eye view of a chariot: axle, cabin, two wheels — くるま. Two millennia later it still parks inside 電車 and 自転車 without a scratch.

lesson_examples.jp: 車（くるま）を　停（と）め　なさい！
トムは　車（くるま）に　乗（の）った。

手.etymology: Pictograph: an open hand seen palm-on — the central stroke is the middle finger, the horizontals the spread of the others. As a left-side component it becomes 扌.
手.mnemonic: Five fingers fanned from a wrist — て. Almost everything you do in Japanese is done 'by hand': 手紙 a letter, 上手 a skilled hand, 歌手 a singer 'of the hand(craft)'.

lesson_examples.jp: 手伝（てつだ）おうか？
lesson_examples.en: Do you want me to help?

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　手（て）が　大（おお）きい。

十.etymology: Originally a single vertical stroke (a needle — the ancestor of 針); a dot, later a crossbar, was added to distinguish it. Borrowed for 'ten': one full crossing of both hands' fingers.
十.mnemonic: A perfect cross: all ten fingers of two open hands meeting at right angles. じゅう — the intersection where the count is complete.

lesson_examples.jp: 十分（じゅうぶん）です。
これは　十分（じゅうぶん）です。

出.etymology: Oracle-bone ideograph: a foot stepping up and out of a pit or dwelling — going out. The later form looks like a sprout growing on past its first frame.
出.mnemonic: One mountain climbing out of another: whatever was inside is on its way out — でる. On every door in Japan: 出口, the way out.

lesson_examples.jp: 元気（げんき）　出（だ）して。
鼻血（はなぢ）　出（で）　てるよ。

女.etymology: Pictograph: a figure kneeling with hands crossed — the posture of a woman in ancient formal dress. The three strokes still trace the crossed arms and folded legs.
女.mnemonic: A dancer mid-curtsy, arms crossing her body — おんな. In compounds she signals the feminine: 女の子, girl; 彼女, she.

lesson_examples.jp: 彼女（かのじょ）は　先生（せんせい）です。
トムの　彼女（かのじょ）って　誰（だれ）？

小.etymology: Ideograph: three tiny points — grains of sand or slivers falling away from a blade. Smallness shown by sheer lack of material.
小.mnemonic: A hook with two shy drops hiding on either side: something so small it barely exists — ちいさい. The vertical stroke is a needle; the drops, its parings.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　手（て）が　小（ちい）さい。
小（ちい）さい　声（こえ）で　話（はな）してください。

上.etymology: Pure ideograph: a short mark placed above a base line. Its twin 下 puts the mark below. Among the oldest abstract signs in the script.
上.mnemonic: A little flag planted on top of the ground line: up, above — うえ. The vertical stroke grows upward like a sapling; nothing hangs below the line.

lesson_examples.jp: 立（た）ち上（あ）がれ！
トムは　上半身（じょうはんしん）　裸（はだか）だ。

人.etymology: Pictograph: a human figure in profile, mid-stride — two legs and a leaning body reduced to two strokes.
人.mnemonic: Two strokes leaning on each other — ひと. The oldest joke in kanji class is also true: people hold each other up. It leans left; its twin 入 (enter) leans in.

lesson_examples.jp: 何人（なんにん）に　話（はな）した？
lesson_examples.en: How many people have you told?

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　いい　人（ひと）だ。

水.etymology: Pictograph: a central current with droplets splashing to both sides. As a left-side component it compresses into the three drops of 氵.
水.mnemonic: A river seen head-on: the main stream down the middle, spray flying left and right — みず. Its on-reading スイ flows through 水曜日, Wednesday, the water day.

lesson_examples.jp: 水（みず）を　ください。
お　水（みず）を　ください。
lesson_examples.en: Can I have some water, please?

生.etymology: Pictograph: a young plant breaking out of the soil — life emerging. Its dozen readings (いきる, うまれる, なま, セイ…) all grow from this one sprout.
生.mnemonic: A seedling standing up out of the ground line — life itself, せい. Raw (なま) like a fresh shoot, born (うまれる) like a first leaf: every reading is this sprout at another age. The 先生 has simply been growing longer.

lesson_examples.jp: 大学生（だいがくせい）です。
彼女（かのじょ）は　先生（せんせい）です。

先.etymology: Compound ideograph: a foot (止, worn to a slanted form) above walking legs (儿) — a footprint out in front of the walker: whoever went ahead, before.
先.mnemonic: Fresh footprints ahead of you on the trail: someone went before — さき. The 先生 is simply the one 'born before' you, walking the path first.

lesson_examples.jp: 彼女（かのじょ）は　先生（せんせい）です。
お　風呂先（ふろさき）に　入（はい）るね。
lesson_examples.en: I'm going to take a bath first.

千.etymology: Formed in oracle-bone script from person (人) + one (一) as a phonetic-numeric device: 'one (unit of) persons' = a thousand.
千.mnemonic: A ten (十) wearing a swept hat: promoted a hundred ranks overnight — せん, one thousand. The hat is the zero-multiplier.

lesson_examples.jp: 千（せん）えん　かします。
lesson_examples.en: I'll lend you a thousand yen.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　千（せん）です。

川.etymology: Pictograph: three lines of flowing water between two banks — a river drawn exactly as it looks from a hill.
川.mnemonic: Three currents running side by side downhill — かわ. The outer strokes are the banks, the middle one the fast water. Found in half the place-names of Japan (小川, 川口).

lesson_examples.jp: 川（かわ）で　およぎます。
これは　川（かわ）です。

足.etymology: Pictograph: the kneecap (the box) above a foot (an old form of 止) — the whole leg. 'To suffice' is an ancient borrowed sense of the same character.
足.mnemonic: A knee, a shin, a foot planted flat — あし. Two of them are plenty: 足りる, 'that's enough legs to stand on'.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　足（あし）が　速（はや）い。
足（あし）の　あざ　どう　したの？
lesson_examples.en: How did you get those bruises on your legs?

大.etymology: Pictograph: a person standing with arms and legs stretched wide — the human body making itself as big as it can.
大.mnemonic: 'How big was the fish?' — arms flung wide: THIS big! おおきい. A stick figure showing off maximum size with its whole body.

lesson_examples.jp: 大（だい）　賛成（さんせい）です。
大学生（だいがくせい）です。

男.etymology: Compound ideograph: rice field (田) + strength/plow (力) — the one whose muscle works the field: a man.
男.mnemonic: Strength (力) under the rice field (田): the farmhand flexing beneath his plot — おとこ. On restroom doors, he's the 男 with the heavy lifting.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　男前（おとこまえ）だ。
トムは　雨（あめ）　男（おとこ）だ。
lesson_examples.en: Every time Tom shows up, it rains.

中.etymology: Ideograph: a pole planted through the exact center of a camp or banner — dead middle. Oracle-bone forms show a flagpole with streamers.
中.mnemonic: An arrow through the bullseye of a target box: right in the middle — なか. In compounds it means 'inside' or 'throughout': 中国, the Middle Country.

lesson_examples.jp: 絶賛（ぜっさん）　放送中（ほうそうちゅう）！
トムは　求職中（きゅうしょくちゅう）だ。
lesson_examples.en: Tom is looking for a job.

天.etymology: Ideograph: a line drawn above the big person (大) — that which stretches over every head: heaven, the sky.
天.mnemonic: The widest thing a person (大) can point at is the line above them: the heavens — てん. 天気 is the sky's mood today.

lesson_examples.jp: 天気（てんき）が　良（よ）かったら　行（い）きます。
lesson_examples.en: I'll go if the weather's good.

lesson_examples.jp: なんか　天気（てんき）　悪（わる）く　なってきたね。
lesson_examples.en: Looks like the weather's gotten worse, eh?

土.etymology: Pictograph: a mound of earth raised on the ground line — the altar of the soil god in its oldest form.
土.mnemonic: A little pile of dirt on the ground with a sprout's cross planted in it — つち. Saturday, 土曜日, is the day you dig in the garden.

lesson_examples.jp: お　土産（みやげ）　何（なん）　買（か）ったの？
lesson_examples.en: What kind of souvenirs did you buy?

lesson_examples.jp: 結婚式（けっこんしき）は　土曜日（どようび）に　行（おこな）われます。
lesson_examples.en: The wedding will take place on Saturday.

二.etymology: Ideograph: two counting rods. The upper stroke is slightly shorter, as when two rods are laid neatly one above the other.
二.mnemonic: Two shelves: a short one on top, a long one below. Count them out loud — に, に — like knocking twice on a door.

lesson_examples.jp: 二人（ににん）とも　ありがとう。
やっと　二人（ににん）に　なれたね。
lesson_examples.en: The two of us are finally alone.

日.etymology: Pictograph: the sun — originally a circle with a dot at its center, squared by the brush into a rectangle with a bar. One sun crossing the sky = one day.
日.mnemonic: A window with the blind half-drawn: through it, the sun. One sunrise per day — ひ, the sun; にち, the day it makes.

lesson_examples.jp: また　明日（あした）。
日本（にっぽん）の　方（ほう）ですか？

入.etymology: Pictograph: a wedge or arrowhead driving inward — or the flap of a tent parting as you step in. The mirror-twin of 人, but leaning the other way.
入.mnemonic: A tent flap pushed open inward: step in — はいる. Watch the lean: 人 walks by, 入 goes in. 入口 is where it happens.

lesson_examples.jp: 目（め）に　何（なに）か　入（はい）った。
lesson_examples.en: I've got something in my eye.

lesson_examples.jp: お　風呂先（ふろさき）に　入（はい）るね。
lesson_examples.en: I'm going to take a bath first.

年.etymology: Oracle-bone ideograph: a person carrying home the ripened grain (禾) — one harvest, one year. The strokes fused over time into the modern form.
年.mnemonic: A farmer bent under a sheaf of rice: another harvest carried home, another year gone — とし. 今年, this crop; 来年, the next.

lesson_examples.jp: 年齢（ねんれい）　聞（き）いても　いいですか？
lesson_examples.en: May I ask how old you are?

lesson_examples.jp: 去年（きょねん）の　クリスマスは　何（なに）　し　てた？
lesson_examples.en: What did you do last Christmas?

白.etymology: Origin debated: commonly explained as a ray of light breaking from the sun (日 with a spark on top), or as a white acorn. Its 'bright, plain' sense is ancient.
白.mnemonic: The first drop of daylight hitting the sun's window at dawn: everything bleaches white — しろ. A sunbeam with the brightness turned all the way up.

lesson_examples.jp: 野球（やきゅう）って　何（なに）が　面白（おもしろ）いの？
白（しろ）　ワインは　お　好（す）きですか？

八.etymology: Ideograph: two strokes leaning away from each other — the act of dividing something in two. Eight is the number you reach by halving three times (2·2·2).
八.mnemonic: Two ski tracks parting on the slope. Divide, divide, divide: 2, 4, 8 — はち. The strokes never touch, like a pie split for sharing.

lesson_examples.jp: りんごが　八（やっ）つ　あります。
八（はち）じに　おきます。

百.etymology: Phono-semantic (形声): one (一) on top for the count, white (白) beneath lending the ancient sound. One 'white' = one hundred.
百.mnemonic: One (一) white (白) hair — the first of a hundred to come, says your grandmother. ひゃく! Count to one hundred and you've earned exactly one white hair.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　百（ひゃく）です。
これは　百円（ひゃく）です。

本.etymology: Ideograph: a tree (木) with a stroke marking its base — the root, the origin. Books came later: the 'root' of knowledge, and paper from the tree itself.
本.mnemonic: Mark the root of the tree: that is where everything begins — もと. From that root comes paper, and from paper the ほん you're reading. 日本: the land at the sun's root.

lesson_examples.jp: これ　誰（だれ）の　本（ほん）？
トムは　本（ほん）の　虫（むし）だ。

名.etymology: Compound ideograph: evening (夕) + mouth (口). In the dark you cannot be seen — so you call out your name to be known.
名.mnemonic: Too dark to see faces at dusk, so a mouth calls into the night: 'It's me!' — your name, なまえ. The password that works when eyes don't.

lesson_examples.jp: トムの　本名（ほんみょう）　知（し）っ　てる？
lesson_examples.en: Do you know Tom's real name?

lesson_examples.jp: ごめん、名前（なまえ）　何（なに）だっけ？

木.etymology: Pictograph: a tree — trunk, spreading branches, roots below. Doubled it becomes a wood (林), tripled a forest (森).
木.mnemonic: Trunk up the middle, branches out, roots down — き. Thursday, 木曜日, is the tree's day. Wherever wood is worked, this kanji stands at the left of the character.

lesson_examples.jp: 今日（きょう）は　木曜日（もくようび）です。
子供（こども）の　ころは　木（き）　登（のぼ）りが　大好（だいす）きでした。
lesson_examples.en: I loved to climb trees when I was a kid.

目.etymology: Pictograph: an eye with its pupil, drawn horizontally on the oracle bones and later stood upright by the brush.
目.mnemonic: An eye standing on end: the two inner bars are the iris and pupil. Stack it next to 日 and 月 — sun, moon, and the め that watches them both.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　目（め）が　青（あお）い。
トムの　目（め）は　青（あお）い。

立.etymology: Pictograph: a person standing squarely on the ground line, arms out for balance — the act of standing itself.
立.mnemonic: Feet planted on the floor line, arms out: stand up! — たつ. A lamp standing at attention on its base; it holds this pose inside 駅 platforms and 立入禁止 signs alike.

lesson_examples.jp: 立（た）ち上（あ）がれ！
トムは　腹（はら）を　立（た）てた。

六.etymology: Originally the pictograph of a small hut with a roof; the word for 'six' was written with it purely for its sound (rebus borrowing).
六.mnemonic: A tiny hut: pointed roof on top, two legs for walls. Six people are crammed inside — ろく, they groan, as the roof creaks.

lesson_examples.jp: 六（むっ）つの　はこが　あります。
これは　六（ろく）です。

音.etymology: Derived from 言 'say' by adding a stroke inside the mouth — sound held in the mouth: tone without words yet.
音.mnemonic: A voice standing (立) on the sun (日), humming with no words — おと. Pure sound, waiting to become speech: turn up the 音楽.

lesson_examples.jp: 今（いま）の　音（おと）　何（なに）？
これ　何（なに）の　音（おと）？

犬.etymology: Pictograph: a dog — the oracle-bone form shows the whole animal; the modern form keeps a big body (大) and one dot for the ear.
犬.mnemonic: A big (大) creature with one flea (the dot) it can't stop scratching — いぬ. Man's best friend, one stroke away from 'big'.

lesson_examples.jp: 犬（いぬ）と　猫（ねこ）　どっちが　好（す）き？
lesson_examples.en: Which do you prefer, dogs or cats?

lesson_examples.jp: これは　犬（いぬ）です。

字.etymology: Compound ideograph: a child (子) raised under a roof (宀). Characters were the 'children' bred in the house of writing — simple signs combined and multiplied.
字.mnemonic: A child under the roof of the schoolhouse, copying its very first letter — ジ. Kanji breed like children: two simple ones move in together and a new 字 is born.

lesson_examples.jp: これ　誰（だれ）の　字（じ）か　分（わ）かる？
lesson_examples.en: Do you know whose handwriting this is?

lesson_examples.jp: トムの　字（じ）って　うまくはないけど　読（よ）み　やすいよね。
lesson_examples.en: Tom's handwriting isn't very good, but it's easy to read.

森.etymology: Compound ideograph: three trees (木) — more trees than a grove (林): a forest.
森.mnemonic: One tree is a tree, two is a grove (林), three is a forest deep enough to get lost in — もり. Count the canopy: the third tree sits on top of the other two.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　森（もり）です。
森（もり）が　すきです。

正.etymology: Compound ideograph: a foot (止) marching straight at a line/target (一) — going straight at it: correct, upright.
正.mnemonic: Walk the straight line without wobbling: that is correct — ただしい. Teachers count scores with this kanji, one stroke per point: five strokes, one 正.

lesson_examples.jp: トムが　正解（せいかい）。
どっちが　正（ただ）しいと　思（おも）う？
lesson_examples.en: Which one do you think is correct?

青.etymology: Compound: a sprout (生, worn down) over a well or mineral vein (丹→月) — the fresh blue-green of plants over deep water. Japanese 青 spans both blue and green.
青.mnemonic: Young shoots reflected in a well: that fresh color between green and blue — あおい. Traffic lights in Japan turn 青 — blue — even when they look green.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　青（あお）ざめた。
トムは　目（め）が　青（あお）い。

赤.etymology: Compound ideograph: a person (大) beside a great fire (火, flattened at the bottom) — skin glowing red in the blaze.
赤.mnemonic: Stand big and close to the bonfire and your face turns red — あかい. A newborn is a 赤ちゃん: red-faced and yelling.

lesson_examples.jp: 顔（かお）　赤（あか）いよ。
この　赤（あか）ちゃんは　生後（せいご）　3週間（しゅうかん）です。

早.etymology: Compound: the sun (日) just clearing the top of a pole (十) — the first hour of daylight: early.
早.mnemonic: The sun climbing the flagpole at dawn while everyone sleeps — はやい. Early and fast are the same kanji: the sun wastes no time.

lesson_examples.jp: 今日（きょう）は　早（はや）く　寝（ね）たいな。
lesson_examples.en: I feel like going to bed early tonight.

lesson_examples.jp: 早（はや）く　しないと　遅（おく）れるよ。
lesson_examples.en: If we don't hurry, we'll be late.

村.etymology: Originally written 邨 (with a phonetic); the modern form is wood (木) + hand-measure (寸) — a settlement measured out in timber.
村.mnemonic: A hand (寸) pacing out plots between the trees (木): here the well, there the houses — a village, むら. Every RPG starts in one.

lesson_examples.jp: 小（ちい）さな　村（むら）に　すんで　います。
lesson_examples.en: I live in a small village.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　村（むら）です。

町.etymology: Phono-semantic: rice field (田) + 丁 (phonetic チョウ) — the raised paths dividing fields into neat blocks; then the blocks of a town.
町.mnemonic: Fields (田) nailed (丁) into a tidy grid of streets — まち. The address system still counts in 丁目: block one, block two.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　町（まち）です。
これは　下町（したまち）です。

田.etymology: Pictograph: a rice paddy seen from above — the box is the dike, the cross the footpaths between plots.
田.mnemonic: A perfect aerial photo of a paddy: four plots, two paths — た. It grows inside half the surnames of Japan: 田中, 山田, 本田.

lesson_examples.jp: ここは　田（た）です。
これは　田舎（いなか）です。

文.etymology: Pictograph: a standing figure with a pattern tattooed on the chest — ornament, pattern, and from there writing and literature.
文.mnemonic: A scholar in a crossed robe, patterns inked on his chest: the first text was worn, not written — ブン. 文学 is that ink grown into literature.

lesson_examples.jp: この　文（ぶん）は　現在（げんざい）　形（かたち）です。
lesson_examples.en: This sentence is in the present tense.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　注文（ちゅうもん）と　違（ちが）います。
lesson_examples.en: This is not what I ordered.

夕.etymology: Pictograph: the crescent moon just risen — half of 月, for the half-lit hour of dusk.
夕.mnemonic: The moon with one stroke still missing: too early for full night — ゆう, the evening. 夕方 is when the sky can't decide.

lesson_examples.jp: 夕食後（ゆうしょくご）は　外出（がいしゅつ）　しては　いけません。
lesson_examples.en: You must not go out after dinner.

lesson_examples.jp: こんな　きれいな　夕陽（ゆうひ）　見（み）た　こと　ないよ。
lesson_examples.en: I've never seen such a beautiful sunset.

力.etymology: Pictograph: a flexed arm with its bulge of muscle — or, by another old reading, a plow biting the earth. Raw strength either way.
力.mnemonic: A bicep curling into a hook — ちから. Wherever it hides in a kanji (男, 助, 動), someone is straining at something.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　全速力（ぜんそくりょく）で　走（はし）った。
力（ちから）に　なれてよかったです。

林.etymology: Compound ideograph: two trees (木) side by side — a stand of trees: a grove. Add a third and it thickens into 森.
林.mnemonic: Two trees planted like neighbors, close enough to share shade — はやし. Halfway between one lonely 木 and the deep 森.

lesson_examples.jp: 林（はやし）の　なかを　あるきます。
これは　林（はやし）です。

王.etymology: Pictograph of a great ceremonial axe, emblem of royal power; the classic reading sees three lines (heaven, humankind, earth) joined by one vertical: the king.
王.mnemonic: Heaven, people, earth — and one stroke holding all three together: that job is the king's — オウ.

lesson_examples.jp: 王（おう）に　あいました。
これは　王様（おうさま）です。

貝.etymology: Pictograph: a cowrie shell with its feelers — cowries were ancient China's money, so 貝 marks value in 買, 貸, 質 and kin.
貝.mnemonic: A shell on two little legs — かい. Wherever 貝 hides in a kanji, money is changing hands.

lesson_examples.jp: はまで　貝（かい）を　あつめます。
lesson_examples.en: I gather shells on the beach.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　貝（かい）です。

玉.etymology: Pictograph: three jade discs strung on a cord; the dot was added to distinguish it from 王 'king'.
玉.mnemonic: The king (王) with one gem in his pocket — たま. Jade beads, rice balls, ten-yen coins: anything round and precious.

lesson_examples.jp: 十円玉（じゅうえんだま）を　いれます。
これは　水玉（みずたま）です。

糸.etymology: Pictograph: a twisted skein of silk. As a left-side component it spins through everything woven, tied or connected (紙, 線, 組).
糸.mnemonic: A silk skein with loose ends dangling — いと. Follow the thread and half the kanji dictionary unravels.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　凧（たこ）に　糸（いと）を　付（つ）けた。
lesson_examples.en: Tom attached the string to the kite.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　糸（いと）です。

石.etymology: Pictograph: a boulder (口) lying at the foot of a cliff (厂) — stone.
石.mnemonic: One rock rolled off the cliff and sat down at the bottom — いし. It's been there since the oracle bones.

lesson_examples.jp: 石鹸（せっけん）が　ありません。
これは　流石（さすが）です。

草.etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 早 'early' (phonetic ソウ) — the green that comes up earliest and everywhere: grass.
草.mnemonic: Up at dawn (早) before anything else in the garden: the weeds — くさ. Grass never sleeps in.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　仕草（しぐさ）です。
まいにち　草臥（くたび）れる。

竹.etymology: Pictograph: two bamboo stalks with drooping leaves. As a crown (⺮) it heads everything once made of bamboo: brushes, boxes, flutes, counting slips.
竹.mnemonic: Two stalks leaning together, leaves like little flags — たけ. Under the bamboo crown, someone is always weaving or counting.

lesson_examples.jp: 竹（たけ）が　あります。
これは　竹（たけ）です。

虫.etymology: Pictograph: originally a coiled viper; the sign broadened to cover every creeping, crawling creature: insects.
虫.mnemonic: A grub standing upright with feelers out — むし. The kanji started as a snake and got demoted to bugs.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　本（ほん）の　虫（むし）だ。
これは　虫（むし）です。

何.etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 可 (phonetic カ). Originally 'to shoulder a load' (the ancestor of 荷); borrowed since antiquity for the question word 'what'.
何.mnemonic: A person stopped by a strange box with a hook: 'What is that?' — なに. The kanji of every beginner's sentence: 何ですか.

lesson_examples.jp: 何（なに）　これ？
何（なに）の　話（はなし）？

会.etymology: Simplified from 會: a lid closing over a layered steamer pot — things coming together as one: to meet.
会.mnemonic: A roof pulled down over rising steam: everyone gathered under one lid — あう. 会社 is where the lid closes on you every morning, カイシャ.

lesson_examples.jp: トムと　会（あ）いたい。
lesson_examples.en: I want to meet with Tom.

lesson_examples.jp: トムに　会（あ）いたい。

外.etymology: Compound ideograph: evening (夕) + divination crack (卜). Divination performed at evening, outside the proper morning ritual — hence 'outside, other'.
外.mnemonic: At dusk (夕) the fortune-teller reads cracks (卜) in a bone by the city gate — outside the walls, where the wild things are: そと, 外国 the lands outside.

lesson_examples.jp: 外（そと）は　雪（ゆき）だよ。
海外（かいがい）　旅行（りょこう）は　初（はじ）めてですか？
lesson_examples.en: Is this your first trip abroad?

間.etymology: Compound ideograph: originally moonlight (月) shining through the crack of a gate (門) — later the sun (日) took the moon's place. The gap itself: interval, in space or time.
間.mnemonic: Sunlight slicing through the gap between two gate doors: that sliver is the interval — あいだ. 時間 measures it in hours, 一週間 in laps of the week.

lesson_examples.jp: 間違（まちが）えました。
ごめん　間違（まちが）えた。

魚.etymology: Pictograph: a whole fish — head at the top (𠂊), scaled body (田), and a tail that later flattened into four dots (灬).
魚.mnemonic: Head, scaly belly, flick of a tail: a fish drawn head-up as if hauled from the water — さかな. The four dots are drops still falling from its fins.

lesson_examples.jp: 魚（さかな）が　います。
これは　魚（さかな）です。

言.etymology: Pictograph: a mouth (口) with sound waves rising from it — speech leaving the lips. As a left-side component it marks nearly everything said in the language.
言.mnemonic: Four sound waves stacked over a mouth: words on their way out — いう. Whenever 言 stands at the left of a kanji, somebody is talking.

lesson_examples.jp: 誰（だれ）にも　言（い）うなよ。
変（へん）な　こと　言（い）うなよ。

古.etymology: Compound ideograph (会意) by the classic account: ten (十) mouths (口) — a story that has passed through ten generations of tellers is old indeed.
古.mnemonic: Ten mouths have told this tale before yours: it is ancient — ふるい. Picture a weathered cross planted over a stone box, standing there for centuries.

lesson_examples.jp: 古（ふる）い　おてらが　あります。
これは　古（ふる）いです。

午.etymology: Pictograph of a wooden pestle, borrowed for the zodiac sign of the Horse — whose hour straddles midday. Hence 'noon': 午前 before it, 午後 after it.
午.mnemonic: A pestle standing bolt upright, like the sun at the top of the sky: noon — ゴ. Morning is 午前, 'before the pestle'; afternoon 午後, 'after it'.

lesson_examples.jp: 午後（ごご）の　会議（かいぎ）、出（で）る？
lesson_examples.en: Are you going to be at this afternoon's meeting?

lesson_examples.jp: 日本（にっぽん）は　今（いま）　午前（ごぜん）　3時（じ）です。

後.etymology: Compound ideograph: a step (彳) hobbled by a small thread (幺) and a dragging foot (夂) — falling behind on the road; hence 'behind' in space and 'after' in time.
後.mnemonic: Shoelace tangled (幺), foot dragging (夂): you fall behind the group — うしろ, and you'll arrive after them — あと, ゴ (午後, the afternoon limping in after noon).

lesson_examples.jp: 午後（ごご）の　会議（かいぎ）、出（で）る？
lesson_examples.en: Are you going to be at this afternoon's meeting?

lesson_examples.jp: 私（わたし）は後（ご）から　行（い）きます。

語.etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 吾 'I, we' (phonetic ゴ) — speech exchanged between me and you: language.
語.mnemonic: My (吾) words (言) — the language I carry: ゴ. It closes the name of every tongue on earth: 日本語, フランス語, and yours next.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　何語（なにご）が　できるの？
lesson_examples.en: What languages do you speak, Tom?

lesson_examples.jp: この　単語（たんご）が　分（わ）かりません。

行.etymology: Pictograph: a crossroads seen from above — both halves are streets. To go is to be out where the roads cross; as a component it flanks kanji of movement.
行.mnemonic: Two street corners facing each other: you're standing in the intersection, already going — いく. 銀行, the bank, sits on the busiest crossroads in town, コウ/ギョウ/いく — a kanji with three lives, all on the move.

lesson_examples.jp: 行（い）くの？
どこ　行（い）くの？

高.etymology: Pictograph: a tall watchtower or gate-building — roof at the top, upper chamber, and the gateway below. 'High' in every later sense, including prices.
高.mnemonic: A pagoda drawn floor by floor: roof, window, gate — たかい. High building, high rank, high price: the tower charges admission.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　声（こえ）が　高（たか）い。
トムは　高血圧（こうけつあつ）だ。

国.etymology: Simplified from 國: a territory enclosed by borders (囗); the modern form places a jewel (玉) inside — the treasure a border exists to guard: a country.
国.mnemonic: A jewel locked inside four walls: the realm and its crown treasure — くに. Line them up: 中国, 外国, and your own 国.

lesson_examples.jp: 中国人（ちゅうごくじん）の　友達（ともだち）は　何人（なんにん）　いますか？
lesson_examples.en: How many Chinese friends do you have?

lesson_examples.jp: 「国連（こくれん）」は「国際（こくさい）　連合（れんごう）」の　略（りゃく）です。

今.etymology: Ideograph: a cover coming down over something — the instant caught and held under the lid: now.
今.mnemonic: A lid snapping shut on the present moment before it escapes — いま. 今日 is today under the lid; 今 is the only kanji you can never write yesterday.

lesson_examples.jp: 今（いま）の　音（おと）　何（なに）？
今週末（こんしゅうまつ）は　暇（ひま）？

時.etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) gives the meaning — time measured by the sun — while 寺 (temple) lends the reading ジ. Temples were the timekeepers, ringing the hours.
時.mnemonic: The temple bell tolls as the sun moves: that is how you know the hour — とき, ジ. 何時ですか — 'what time is it?' asks the sun of the temple.

lesson_examples.jp: もう　11時（じ）だよ。
いま　何時（なんじ）ですか？

社.etymology: Compound ideograph: altar (示, compressed to ネ) + soil (土) — the shrine of the local earth god, where the community gathered. From 'gathered community' came 'society' and 'company'.
社.mnemonic: An altar planted in the village soil: the whole community assembles there — シャ. Today the assembly wears suits: 会社. The gods kept the original office: 神社.

lesson_examples.jp: 会社（かいしゃ）で　はたらきます。
これは　弊社（へいしゃ）です。

週.etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 周 'circuit, all around' (phonetic シュウ) — going one full round. Applied to the seven-day cycle when Japan adopted the Western week.
週.mnemonic: Walk one full lap (周) around the calendar and you're back where you started: one week — シュウ. 毎週, every lap.

lesson_examples.jp: 今週末（こんしゅうまつ）は　暇（ひま）？
今週末（こんしゅうまつ）　空（あ）い　てる？

examples.reading: みぶんしょうめいしょ

書.etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand gripping a brush (聿) over a tablet (the 日-shaped block below) — the act of writing caught mid-stroke.
書.mnemonic: A hand pressing a brush down onto the page, line after line — かく. The stacked horizontals are the ruled lines of the notebook; 図書館 keeps what the brush leaves behind.

lesson_examples.jp: 何（なに）　書（か）いてんの？
ペンで　書（か）いて下（くだ）さい。

少.etymology: Derived from 小 (small) with an extra stroke shaving something off — smaller still in quantity: few, scarce.
少.mnemonic: Take 'small' (小) and slice one more piece off with a diagonal cut: now there's hardly any left — すこし, すくない.

lesson_examples.jp: 少々（しょうしょう）　お　まち　ください。
ほんの　少（すこ）し　ください。

食.etymology: Pictograph: a lid (𠆢) over a full food vessel on its stand — a covered dish waiting to be eaten. The component form 飠 fronts most kanji of eating.
食.mnemonic: Lift the lid: dinner is served — たべる. Everything under that little roof is on the menu; 食べ物 is whatever the lid was hiding.

lesson_examples.jp: 何（なに）　食（た）べたい？
lesson_examples.en: What do you want to eat?

lesson_examples.jp: 何（なに）を　食（た）べた？

新.etymology: Phono-semantic: 亲 (a standing tree, phonetic シン) + axe (斤) — wood at the instant the axe cuts it: fresh, new.
新.mnemonic: The axe bites and the pale fresh grain gleams where the bark fell away: brand-new — あたらしい. 新聞: the news, cut fresh every morning.

lesson_examples.jp: 新聞（しんぶん）　どこ？
新入生（しんにゅうせい）の　方（ほう）ですか？

西.etymology: Traditionally: a bird settling into its nest — which birds do at sundown, in the direction of the setting sun: west. The oldest forms show a woven nest or basket.
西.mnemonic: A bird folding itself into a basket-nest as the sun drops behind it: face that glow and you face west — にし. 関西 lies that way from Tokyo.

lesson_examples.jp: 西（にし）へ　いきます。
これは　新西蘭（にゅーじーらんど）です。

前.etymology: Originally a foot aboard a boat gliding forward — 'to advance'; the blade (刂) entered the character early as a graphic-phonetic addition. 'In front, before' is the settled meaning.
前.mnemonic: On the prow of the boat, blade in hand, cutting the water ahead: everything in front of you — まえ. 名前 puts your name out front for the world.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　男前（おとこまえ）だ。
前（まえ）に　進（すす）んでください。

多.etymology: Compound ideograph: two evenings (夕) stacked — night after night after night. Repetition itself made visible: many.
多.mnemonic: Two crescent moons piled up like plates after a feast: one evening wasn't enough, there were many — おおい. Stack anything twice in kanji and it multiplies.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　多分（たぶん）　大丈夫（だいじょうぶ）。
トムは　多分（たぶん）　待（ま）っている。

長.etymology: Pictograph: an elder with long flowing hair leaning on a staff — long in hair, long in years; and the eldest leads, hence 'chief'.
長.mnemonic: Hair so long it takes six strokes, and a cane to match — ながい. The one who's been here longest sits at the head of the table: 社長, 校長.

lesson_examples.jp: 身長（しんちょう）　何（なん）センチ？
長（なが）い　一週間（いちしゅうかん）だったな。

店.etymology: Phono-semantic: a building with a canopy (广) + 占 'occupy a spot' (phonetic テン) — a stall pitched under an awning that claimed its corner: a shop.
店.mnemonic: Under the awning, a fortune-teller (占) set up shop and never left — みせ. The 喫茶店 on the corner has occupied that spot forever.

lesson_examples.jp: スーパーは　10時（じ）に　開店（かいてん）　します。
lesson_examples.en: The supermarket opens at ten o'clock.

lesson_examples.jp: これが　店（みせ）で　一番（いちばん）　いい　カメラです。
lesson_examples.en: This is the best camera in the store.

電.etymology: Compound: rain (雨) over a lightning bolt with a trailing tail (an old form of 申, itself a pictograph of forked lightning). First 'lightning', then 'electricity'.
電.mnemonic: Out of the storm cloud, a bolt with a hooked tail — raw electricity: デン. It powers the whole modern lexicon: 電気, 電車, 電話.

lesson_examples.jp: 電話（でんわ）　して。
トムに　電話（でんわ）　して。

東.etymology: Traditionally explained as the sun (日) rising behind a tree (木) — the east. Paleographers read the oldest form as a tied sack, borrowed for its sound; the sunrise story is what stuck.
東.mnemonic: The sun climbing up through the branches of a tree at dawn: look that way and you face east — ひがし. 東京: the capital of the east.

lesson_examples.jp: 東（ひがし）の　そらが　あかるい。
これは　東（ひがし）です。

道.etymology: Compound ideograph: movement (辶) + head (首) — walking with your head leading you: the road you follow, and figuratively the Way (as in 柔道, 茶道).
道.mnemonic: Your head out in front, feet rolling beneath it down the path — みち. Every martial art ends in this kanji: the road you walk your whole life, ドウ.

lesson_examples.jp: ここ　通（とお）った　こと　ない　道（みち）だよね？
lesson_examples.en: We've never gone this way, have we?

lesson_examples.jp: オーストラリアの　水道水（すいどうすい）は　飲（の）める　んですか？
lesson_examples.en: Is the tap water in Australia drinkable?

読.etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 売 'sell' (simplified from 賣, the old phonetic ドク/トク) — words offered up like wares, taken in by reading.
読.mnemonic: A street seller (売) hawking words (言) aloud — and you, reading the signboard: よむ. 読書 is buying stories with your eyes.

lesson_examples.jp: 何（なに）　読（よ）ん　でるの？
トムは　本（ほん）を　読（よ）んでいる。

南.etymology: Origin debated — the oldest forms show a hanging bell or a tent; the classic account reads it as a shelter whose opening faces the warm side. Whatever the picture, it has meant 'south' for three millennia.
南.mnemonic: A greenhouse with its door thrown open to the sun's warm side: plants crowding toward the south — みなみ. 東南アジア: where that warmth lives year-round.

lesson_examples.jp: 南（みなみ）の　まちへ　いきます。
lesson_examples.en: I'm heading to a southern town.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　南（みなみ）です。

買.etymology: Compound ideograph: a net (罒) over a cowrie shell (貝, ancient money) — netting goods with money: to buy.
買.mnemonic: Casting a net straight over the treasure shell: haul it in, it's yours — かう. 買い物: hunting with a wallet for a net.

lesson_examples.jp: 何（なに）　買（か）ったの？
お　土産（みやげ）　何（なん）　買（か）ったの？
lesson_examples.en: What kind of souvenirs did you buy?

半.etymology: Compound ideograph: divide (八) atop an ox (牛) — an ox split down the middle for sharing: half.
半.mnemonic: The ox chopped clean in two — each side gets half, はん. Clock language lives here: 三時半, half past three.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　上半身（じょうはんしん）　裸（はだか）だ。
誰（だれ）か　2時半（じはん）に　起（お）こして。
lesson_examples.en: Would someone please wake me up at 2:30?

父.etymology: Pictograph: a hand gripping a stone axe — the provider and protector of the household: father.
父.mnemonic: Crossed arms holding two axes: dad guarding the door — ちち. Address him gently and he softens to お父さん.

lesson_examples.jp: お父（とう）さんは　お　元気（げんき）ですか？
お　父様（とうさま）は　何（なに）を　なさっている　んですか？

分.etymology: Compound ideograph: divide (八) + sword (刀) — a blade splitting something in two: a part. An hour cut into sixty parts gives the minute; a thing cut open gives understanding (分かる).
分.mnemonic: The sword slices the pie in two — one part for you, ブン. Slice the hour: minutes, フン. Slice a problem open: 分かった, got it!

lesson_examples.jp: 十分（じゅうぶん）です。
分（わ）かってます。

聞.etymology: Phono-semantic: ear (耳) inside gate (門, phonetic モン→ブン) — an ear pressed to the gate: to hear; and, in Japanese, to ask.
聞.mnemonic: An ear flattened against the gate, catching every word from the other side — きく. To hear is half of it; the nosy half is to ask. 新聞: everything the ear at the gate collected, printed by morning.

lesson_examples.jp: 新聞（しんぶん）　どこ？
聞（き）こえますか。

母.etymology: Pictograph: the woman sign (女) with two dots added for the breasts — a nursing mother. One of the most transparent kanji in the script.
母.mnemonic: A woman with two dots: the mother who nursed you — はは. The frame around the dots is her embrace; every stroke leans inward, protective.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　母親（ははおや）　似（に）だ。
母（はは）は　弁護士（べんごし）です。

北.etymology: Compound ideograph: two people sitting back to back — the origin of 背 'back'. In a south-facing culture, north is the direction at everyone's back.
北.mnemonic: Two travelers huddle back to back against the cold wind: they're facing away from the north — きた. 北海道 is where they huddle hardest.

lesson_examples.jp: 北（きた）へ　いきます。
これは　北（きた）です。

毎.etymology: Originally the mother sign (母) crowned with a hairpin or sprout — fertile, ever-producing growth; borrowed early for 'every, each'.
毎.mnemonic: A mother with a feather in her hair, up at dawn without fail: every single day — まい. 毎日, 毎週, 毎年: she never misses one.

lesson_examples.jp: 姉（あね）は　毎日（まいにち）　ジョギングを　しています。
lesson_examples.en: My older sister goes jogging every day.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　毎週（まいしゅう）です。

万.etymology: Simplification of 萬, originally the pictograph of a scorpion, borrowed since antiquity for the number 10,000.
万.mnemonic: A scorpion with its tail curled — count its swarm of eggs: ten thousand, まん. In prices it swings that tail through your wallet: 一万円.

lesson_examples.jp: 一万（いちまん）えん　あります。
これは　万全（ばんぜん）です。

友.etymology: Compound ideograph: two right hands reaching the same way — hands joined in common work: a friend.
友.mnemonic: Two hands stacked in a team huddle — とも. A 友だち is the hand that shows up when yours is full.

lesson_examples.jp: 中国人（ちゅうごくじん）の　友達（ともだち）は　何人（なんにん）　いますか？
lesson_examples.en: How many Chinese friends do you have?

lesson_examples.jp: カナダ人（じん）の　友達（ともだち）は　何人（なんにん）　いますか？
lesson_examples.en: How many Canadian friends do you have?

来.etymology: Simplified from 來, the pictograph of a ripened wheat plant. Legend held that wheat 'came from heaven' — so the grain sign was borrowed for 'to come' and never given back.
来.mnemonic: A wheat stalk waving you over from the field's edge: come! — くる. What is on its way is 来る; next year, 来年, is already walking toward you.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　もう　来（き）た？
ここ　よく　来（く）るの？

話.etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + tongue (舌, from an older phonetic) — the tongue shaping words into a story or conversation.
話.mnemonic: Words (言) rolled off a tongue (舌) and braided into a tale — はなし. Phone conversations are 電話: electric talk.

lesson_examples.jp: 何（なに）の　話（はなし）？
電話（でんわ）　して。

引.etymology: Compound ideograph: a bow (弓) plus a single vertical stroke — the string drawn back: to pull.
引.mnemonic: Grab the bowstring (the lone stroke) and pull the bow (弓) to full stretch — ひく. Doors in Japan tell you which side does it: 引 pull, 押 push.

lesson_examples.jp: 風邪（かぜ）　引（ひ）かない　ようにね。
風邪（かぜ）　引（ひ）くから　早（はや）く　服（ふく）　着（き）　なさい。
lesson_examples.en: Put some clothes on, you'll catch a cold.

遠.etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 袁 'long flowing robe' (phonetic エン) — a walk so long you need your traveling robe: distant.
遠.mnemonic: Hitch up the long robe and start walking: it's far — とおい. 遠足 is the school excursion that never seems to end.

lesson_examples.jp: 明日（あした）が　待（ま）ち遠（どお）しいよ。
lesson_examples.en: I can hardly wait until tomorrow.

lesson_examples.jp: 明日（あした）の　夜（よる）が　待（ま）ち遠（どお）しいです。
lesson_examples.en: I'm looking forward to tomorrow night.

夏.etymology: Pictograph: a grand masked dancer — a great head with trailing legs (夂) — from the midsummer festival dances of ancient China.
夏.mnemonic: A masked dancer stamping slow steps in the heat of the festival night — なつ. Summer is when the mask comes out and the legs drag.

lesson_examples.jp: 早（はや）く　夏休（なつやす）みに　ならないかなあ。
lesson_examples.en: I wish summer break would hurry up and get here.

lesson_examples.jp: 夏休（なつやす）みは　どこかへ　行（い）きましたか。
lesson_examples.en: Did you go anywhere during the summer vacation?

家.etymology: Compound ideograph: a pig (豕) under a roof (宀) — livestock beneath the family roof was the ancient household's wealth: home.
家.mnemonic: A pig snoring under the roof: the house is doing well — いえ. Home is where the bacon sleeps; the ~カ ending also names the expert 'of the house': 作家, 画家.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　策略家（さくりゃくか）だ。
うちは　4人（にん）　家族（かぞく）です。
lesson_examples.en: There are four people in my family.

歌.etymology: Phono-semantic: 哥 (two 可, phonetic カ) + 欠, the wide-open mouth — breath pouring out in melody: song.
歌.mnemonic: Two karaoke prompts (可可) and a mouth thrown wide open (欠) — うた! The 歌手 holds the note; you hold the remote.

lesson_examples.jp: この　歌（うた）　知（し）っ　てる？
好（す）きな　歌手（かしゅ）とか　いる？
lesson_examples.en: Do you have a favorite singer?

画.etymology: Simplified from 畫: a hand with a brush (聿) drawing the boundaries of a field (田) — to draw; a drawn stroke; a picture.
画.mnemonic: A framed field hung on the wall: the first landscape painting — ガ. Movies are 映画, moving pictures; each kanji stroke is one 画.

lesson_examples.jp: 最近（さいきん）　何（なに）か　映画（えいが）　見（み）た？
映画館（えいがかん）は　駅（えき）から　近（ちか）いの？
lesson_examples.en: Is the movie theater near the station?

回.etymology: Pictograph: a spiral, squared by the brush into a box within a box — turning around, a revolution, hence a counter for repetitions.
回.mnemonic: A whirlpool drawn with a ruler: around and around — まわる. Each full loop counts one time: 一回, 二回, 三回.

lesson_examples.jp: もう　一回（いちかい）　やってみて。
トムは　頭（あたま）の　回転（かいてん）が　速（はや）い。
lesson_examples.en: Tom has a good head on his shoulders.

海.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 毎 'every' (phonetic カイ) — the water every river runs home to: the sea.
海.mnemonic: Every (毎) drop of water (氵) ends up in the same place — うみ. Mother ocean: look closely, 母 is sitting inside 毎.

lesson_examples.jp: 海外（かいがい）　旅行（りょこう）は　初（はじ）めてですか？
lesson_examples.en: Is this your first trip abroad?

lesson_examples.jp: 誰（だれ）か　海（うみ）まで　散歩（さんぽ）に　行（い）かない？
lesson_examples.en: Anybody want to take a walk to the sea?

楽.etymology: Simplified from 樂: a great drum hung with bells on a wooden stand (木) — music; and the ease and pleasure music brings.
楽.mnemonic: A festival drum on its wooden stand, bells jingling on both sides — music, ガク; and the crowd's face: 楽しい, たのしい. One kanji, both the song and the smile.

lesson_examples.jp: 趣味（しゅみ）は　音楽（おんがく）　鑑賞（かんしょう）です。
lesson_examples.en: My hobby is listening to music.

lesson_examples.jp: 音楽（おんがく）は　お　好（す）きですか？

顔.etymology: Phono-semantic: 彦 'handsome young man' (phonetic ガン) + 頁 'head' — the front of the head at its most presentable: the face.
顔.mnemonic: The handsome one (彦) turns his head (頁) toward the camera: that's the face — かお. 顔 is what 洗顔 washes and 笑顔 lights up.

lesson_examples.jp: 顔（かお）　赤（あか）いよ。
トムは　顔（かお）が　広（ひろ）い。
lesson_examples.en: Tom knows a lot of people.

帰.etymology: Simplified from 歸: troops (𠂤) coming back to the wife's broom (帚) — the soldier returning to swept floors: to go home.
帰.mnemonic: The sword hung up at the door, the broom waiting inside: homecoming — かえる. ただいま! is this kanji spoken aloud.

lesson_examples.jp: いつ　帰（かえ）ってくるの？
トムは　もう　家（いえ）に　帰（かえ）った。

牛.etymology: Pictograph: an ox head seen from the front — the top strokes are the horns, the vertical its long face.
牛.mnemonic: Face-to-face with an ox: one horn up, ears out, the long nose down the middle — うし. 牛乳 is what it gives; 牛肉 is what it becomes.

lesson_examples.jp: 牛（うし）が　います。
牛（うし）の　ミルクを　のみます。

京.etymology: Pictograph: a tall building raised on high ground — the watchtower of the royal city: the capital.
京.mnemonic: A palace tower on the hill, visible for miles: you've reached the capital — キョウ. It anchors both 東京 and 京都 — the new capital and the old.

lesson_examples.jp: 京（きょう）へ　いきます。
これは　東京（とうきょう）です。

強.etymology: Originally the name of a hard-shelled weevil; borrowed early for 彊 'powerful bow'. The bow (弓) stayed on as the character's anchor of meaning.
強.mnemonic: A bow (弓) so taut even the armored beetle (虫) bounces off — つよい. 勉強, studying, is this strength applied to your own skull.

lesson_examples.jp: トムが　最強（さいきょう）。
トムは　責任感（せきにんかん）が　強（つよ）い。
lesson_examples.en: Tom has a strong sense of responsibility.

教.etymology: Compound: a child (子) under crossed counting-sticks (爻), with the master's hand holding a rod (攵) — instruction, old style: to teach.
教.mnemonic: The old master taps the board, the child copies the crossed strokes — おしえる. 教室 is the room where the tapping happens.

lesson_examples.jp: トム、メアド　教（おし）えて。
住所（じゅうしょ）を　教（おし）えてください。

近.etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 斤 'axe' (phonetic キン) — within walking distance of the sound of the axe: near.
近.mnemonic: If you can hear the axe chopping, you're almost there — ちかい. 近所 is everything within one axe-echo of your door.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　近（ちか）くに　いる？
最近（さいきん）　何（なに）か　映画（えいが）　見（み）た？

兄.etymology: Compound ideograph: a mouth (口) on legs (儿) — the sibling old enough to speak for the others: the elder brother.
兄.mnemonic: A walking mouth that never stops giving orders — あに. Politely he's お兄さん; in the kanji he's still just a bossy mouth on legs.

lesson_examples.jp: 兄（あに）は　ボストンに　住（す）んでいます。
lesson_examples.en: My brother is living in Boston.

lesson_examples.jp: 兄（あに）は　今（こん）　オーストラリアに　います。
lesson_examples.en: My brother is in Australia now.

計.etymology: Compound ideograph: words (言) + ten (十) — counting out loud to ten: to reckon, measure, plan.
計.mnemonic: Count to ten before you act — that's a plan, ケイ. The 時計 on your wrist counts for you, all day long.

lesson_examples.jp: 熱（ねつ）　計（はか）ってみたら？
lesson_examples.en: Why don't you take your temperature?

lesson_examples.jp: 時計（とけい）を　なくしました。

元.etymology: Pictograph: a person (儿) with the head emphasized by two strokes — the head as the origin-point of the body: beginning, source.
元.mnemonic: A pair of legs carrying the 'first thing' on top: the head, where everything starts — もと. 元気 is your original energy, factory settings restored.

lesson_examples.jp: 元気（げんき）　出（だ）して。
元気（げんき）　出（だ）しなよ。

光.etymology: Compound ideograph: fire (火, flattened) carried on a person's legs (儿) — a torch-bearer: light on the move, rays.
光.mnemonic: A runner carrying the torch through the dark, sparks streaming — ひかり. Light with legs: that's a ray.

lesson_examples.jp: 光（ひかり）が　きれいです。
まいにち　光（ひか）る。

工.etymology: Pictograph: a carpenter's square or work-tool — craft, work, construction. One of the oldest tool-signs in the script.
工.mnemonic: An I-beam standing in the frame of a building site — コウ. Wherever 工 appears (工事, 工場), someone in a helmet is measuring twice.

lesson_examples.jp: 父（ちち）は 大工（だいく）です。
これは　細工（さいく）です。

広.etymology: Simplified from 廣: a building (广) with a vast interior (the phonetic 黄 reduced to 厶) — a roomy hall: wide, spacious.
広.mnemonic: Under one roof, so much empty floor that a single elbow (厶) rattles around in it — ひろい. 広場: the wide-open plaza.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　顔（かお）が　広（ひろ）い。
lesson_examples.en: Tom knows a lot of people.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　広大（こうだい）です。

考.etymology: Phono-semantic: an old man (耂) + a bent breath-stroke (丂, phonetic コウ) — the elder bent over a question: to ponder.
考.mnemonic: The old master strokes his beard, thoughts bending like the bottom stroke — かんがえる. Real thinking has a crook in it.

lesson_examples.jp: 考（かんが）えすぎだよ。
何（なに）　考（かんが）え　てるの？

合.etymology: Compound ideograph: a lid (亼) settling onto a mouth or vessel (口) — two halves made for each other: to fit, to match.
合.mnemonic: The lid clicks perfectly onto the jar — あう. Whatever matches, matches here: 試合 a match of players, 都合 a match of schedules.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　具合（ぐあい）が　悪（わる）そうだ。
集合（しゅうごう）　場所（ばしょ）は　どこですか？

黒.etymology: Simplified from 黑: a chimney vent blackened by the fire (灬) burning below — soot: black.
黒.mnemonic: Look up the chimney over the flames: everything the smoke touched is black — くろい. The four dots are the fire still cooking the soot.

lesson_examples.jp: 黒（くろ）い　のが　私（わたし）　のです。
トムは　髪（かみ）を　黒（くろ）く　染（そ）めた。

作.etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 乍 'to hew, notch' (phonetic サク) — a person cutting something into shape: to make.
作.mnemonic: A craftsman notching wood, chip by chip, until the thing exists — つくる. The 作家 hews sentences instead.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　作（つく）り笑（わら）いを　した。
好（す）きな　作家（さっか）は　誰（だれ）ですか？

姉.etymology: Phono-semantic: woman (女) + a right side descended from an old phonetic (written like 市 'market' today) — the elder sister.
姉.mnemonic: The young woman (女) sent to the market (市) with the family purse: responsibility means you're the elder sister — あね, お姉さん.

lesson_examples.jp: 姉（あね）は　毎日（まいにち）　ジョギングを　しています。
lesson_examples.en: My older sister goes jogging every day.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　姉（あね）です。

市.etymology: Pictograph: a pole with a banner (亠) raised over cloth stalls (巾) — the sign that market day is on; later the market town, the city.
市.mnemonic: Raise the flag over the cloth stalls and the whole town gathers — いち, the market; シ, the city it grew into (広島市, 京都市).

lesson_examples.jp: 市役所前（しやくしょまえ）の　パン屋（や）さんが　値上（ねあ）げ　し　てた。
lesson_examples.en: The baker in front of City Hall increased his prices.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　市場（いちば）です。

思.etymology: Compound ideograph: originally the fontanelle/brain (囟, later confused with 田) over the heart (心) — brain and heart working together: to think, to feel.
思.mnemonic: The field on top is your brain's little plot; the heart below waters it — おもう. In Japanese you think with both: と思います.

lesson_examples.jp: 私（わたし）も　そう　思（おも）う。
トムは　どう　思（おも）う？

止.etymology: Pictograph: a footprint — the foot planted: to stop. As a component it walks through 歩, 正, 歴 and dozens more.
止.mnemonic: A foot slammed flat on the ground: halt! — とまる. Red sign in Japan: 止まれ. The footprint that refuses to move.

lesson_examples.jp: 息（いき）を　止（と）めてください。
この　付近（ふきん）は　駐車（ちゅうしゃ）　禁止（きんし）です。

紙.etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 氏 (phonetic シ) — sheets felted from silk and plant fiber: paper, which China invented from exactly that.
紙.mnemonic: Mash the fibers (糸) flat and let them dry into a sheet — かみ. A 手紙 is fiber that carries your handwriting across the country.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　手紙（てがみ）を　燃（も）やした。
こちらの　用紙（ようし）に　記入（きにゅう）　してください。

自.etymology: Pictograph: a nose seen from the front. To this day Japanese speakers point at their nose to say 'me?' — oneself.
自.mnemonic: Point at your own nose: me, myself — ジ. Everything automatic (自動), self-made (自分) or free-willed (自由) starts at the nose.

lesson_examples.jp: この　自転車（じてんしゃ）、誰（だれ）の？
これ　自分（じぶん）で　描（えが）いたの？

室.etymology: Phono-semantic: roof (宀) + 至 'to arrive' (phonetic シツ) — the space under the roof you arrive into: a room.
室.mnemonic: Walk under the roof until you can go no further (至): you've arrived in the room — シツ. The 教室 is the room the school day arrives at.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　和室（わしつ）です。
これは　温室効果（おんしつこうかがす）ガスです。

弱.etymology: Compound: two bows (弓) with soft frayed decorations hanging from them — ornamental bows never meant to fire: weak.
弱.mnemonic: Two ceremonial bows dripping with tassels: pretty, useless in a fight — よわい. Twice the bows, half the strength.

lesson_examples.jp: よわねを　はかず、弱（よわ）さと　むきあう。
まいにち　弱（よわ）る。

首.etymology: Pictograph: a head with its hair (the top strokes) and its face reduced to an eye — the head, and by extension the neck it sits on.
首.mnemonic: Hair on top, eye in the middle: a head planted on a neck — くび. The 首相 is the 'neck minister': the head of government.

lesson_examples.jp: きりんは　首（くび）が　ながいです。
首（くび）が　いたいです。

秋.etymology: Compound ideograph: grain (禾) + fire (火) — the stubble fires burning after harvest: autumn.
秋.mnemonic: The harvest is in and the fields are set alight; smoke and gold everywhere — あき. Autumn is grain plus flame.

lesson_examples.jp: 春（はる）と　秋（あき）では　どっちが　好（す）き？
lesson_examples.en: Which do you prefer, spring or autumn?

lesson_examples.jp: これは　秋（あき）です。

春.etymology: Compound: sprouts pushing up (an old form of 屯, worn into 三 + 人) under the sun (日) — the season of germination: spring.
春.mnemonic: Three shoots and a pair of legs racing up toward the sun — はる. Spring is the ground sprinting.

lesson_examples.jp: 春（はる）と　秋（あき）では　どっちが　好（す）き？
lesson_examples.en: Which do you prefer, spring or autumn?

lesson_examples.jp: 春巻（はるま）きってなんで　春巻（はるま）きっていうか　知（し）っ　てる？
lesson_examples.en: Do you know why spring rolls are called spring rolls?

場.etymology: Phono-semantic: soil (土) + 昜 'sun rising high' (phonetic ジョウ) — sunlit ground: an open place, a site.
場.mnemonic: A patch of earth the sun picks out like a spotlight: the place where things happen — ば. 場所, 工場, 野球場 — every stage is soil plus light.

lesson_examples.jp: 入場料（にゅうじょうりょう）は　いくらですか？
入場券（にゅうじょうけん）は　いくらですか？
lesson_examples.en: How much is the entrance fee?

色.etymology: Compound: two bent human figures pressed together — originally facial flush and passion; from the color of the face came 'color' itself.
色.mnemonic: A blush spreading over a face: the first color anyone notices — いろ. Feelings leak out as colors; that's why 色 means both.

lesson_examples.jp: 顔色（かおいろ）　悪（わる）いけど　大丈夫（だいじょうぶ）？ 　病院（びょういん）　行（い）った　方（ほう）が　いい　んじゃない？
lesson_examples.en: Your face looks pale. Are you OK? Maybe it would be better if you went to the hospital, don't you think?

lesson_examples.jp: すきな　色（いろ）は　なんですか。

心.etymology: Pictograph: the heart organ with its chambers — three drops of blood around the central hook. As a component (心/忄) it beats inside every kanji of feeling.
心.mnemonic: A heart mid-beat, blood flying — こころ. Find it at the bottom of 思, 悪, 意: whatever the top does, the heart underneath feels it.

lesson_examples.jp: 心配（しんぱい）　しないで。
何（なに）が　心配（しんぱい）なの？

親.etymology: Phono-semantic: 亲 (a standing tree, phonetic シン) + 見 'watch' — the classic image: the parent up the tree, watching for the child's return.
親.mnemonic: Climbed up the tree (亲), eyes on the road (見), waiting for you to come home — おや. That worried silhouette is what 'parent' looks like.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　母親（ははおや）　似（に）だ。
親（おや）には　もう　話（はな）しました。

図.etymology: Simplified from 圖: a bordered territory (囗) with its granaries and roads sketched inside — a plan, a map.
図.mnemonic: A framed sheet with X-marks-the-spot scratched inside: the map — ズ. The 図書館 shelves whole worlds folded flat.

lesson_examples.jp: 25ページの　地図（ちず）を　見（み）てください。
lesson_examples.en: Look at the map on page 25.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　図（はか）る。

声.etymology: Simplified from 聲: a hanging stone chime being struck, with an ear listening below — ringing sound: the voice.
声.mnemonic: A stone chime hangs from its frame; strike it and it answers — こえ. Your voice is the chime only you can ring.

lesson_examples.jp: トムの　声（こえ）が　する。
トムは　声（こえ）が　高（たか）い。

切.etymology: Phono-semantic: 七 (originally the picture of cutting crosswise, phonetic セツ) + 刀 'sword' — the blade doing what 七 once drew: to cut.
切.mnemonic: Seven (七) slices of the sword (刀) — きる. 切符 is a ticket cut from the roll; 大切 is what you'd never let be cut away.

lesson_examples.jp: 切符（きっぷ）を　見（み）せてください。
トムは　通（とお）りを　横切（よこぎ）った。

走.etymology: Compound ideograph: a person leaning into a sprint (worn into 土) over a flying foot (止) — arms pumping: to run.
走.mnemonic: Torso pitched forward, one foot barely touching ground — はしる. The whole kanji is mid-stride; that's why nothing in it stands straight.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　全速力（ぜんそくりょく）で　走（はし）った。
まいにち　走（はし）る。

太.etymology: Derived from 大 'big' with a dot added for emphasis — bigger than big: thick, stout.
太.mnemonic: 'Big' (大) after dessert: one extra dot at the belly — ふとい. The 太陽, the sun, is the plumpest thing in the sky.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　太（ふと）った。
私（わたし）って　太（ふと）っ　てると　思（おも）う？

体.etymology: Modern form of 體: person (亻) + 本 'root' — the body as a person's root and trunk, the base everything else grows from.
体.mnemonic: Your body is the root (本) your person (亻) is planted in — からだ. Take care of the trunk before decorating the branches.

lesson_examples.jp: トムの　容体（ようだい）が　悪化（あっか）　した。
これは　体付（からだつ）きです。

台.etymology: Adopted as the simple form of 臺 'raised tower' — an old character combining 厶 and 口, long used for platforms and stands; now also the counter for machines.
台.mnemonic: A little podium: base block (口) with a speaker's arm (厶) resting on top — ダイ. Machines get counted on pedestals: 一台, 二台.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　台所（だいどころ）だよ。
それは　こっちの　台詞（だいし）だよ。

知.etymology: Compound ideograph: arrow (矢) + mouth (口) — an answer that flies from the mouth straight as an arrow: to know.
知.mnemonic: Ask, and the reply hits the bullseye before you finish the question — しる. Knowledge is a mouth with good aim.

lesson_examples.jp: 知（し）らなかったの？
この　歌（うた）　知（し）っ　てる？

地.etymology: Phono-semantic: soil (土) + 也 (phonetic チ) — the ground underfoot; the earth as terrain rather than dirt.
地.mnemonic: Soil (土) stretching away in a long winding tail (也): the land itself — チ. 地図 maps it, 地下鉄 tunnels under it.

lesson_examples.jp: 25ページの　地図（ちず）を　見（み）てください。
lesson_examples.en: Look at the map on page 25.

lesson_examples.jp: もしも　地球（ちきゅう）の　自転（じてん）が　止（と）まったら　どう　なると　思（おも）う？
lesson_examples.en: What do you think would happen if the earth stopped spinning?

池.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 也 (phonetic チ) — water gathered in a hollow of the ground: a pond. The twin of 地 with water swapped for soil.
池.mnemonic: Same winding hollow as 地, but filled with water (氵): the garden pond — いけ. Where 地 ends, 池 reflects.

lesson_examples.jp: その　池（いけ）は　深（ふか）さ　3　mです。
こんな　ところに　池（いけ）が　あるなんて　知（し）らなかった。
lesson_examples.en: I didn't know there was a pond here.

茶.etymology: Variant of the older 荼: the plant (艹) over a phonetic reduced to a canopy on a tree-like base — the tea bush, and the drink that conquered the world.
茶.mnemonic: A leaf (艹) drying under a little canopy on a wooden rack: tea in the making — チャ. お茶 time is when the kanji finally gets poured.

lesson_examples.jp: お茶（ちゃ）を　もらえますか。
お茶（ちゃ）を　もう少（すこ）し　下（くだ）さい。

昼.etymology: Simplified from 晝: a hand with a brush (聿) ruling off the hours of the sun (日) — the measured stretch of daylight: daytime.
昼.mnemonic: A ruler laid across the sun: the bright hours, measured from bell to bell — ひる. 昼ご飯 lands exactly in the middle of the ruler.

lesson_examples.jp: お昼（ひる）は　もう　食（た）べたよ。
まだ　お昼（ひる）　食（た）べ　てないの？

朝.etymology: Compound ideograph: the sun (日) rising through grass (the vertical strokes) while the moon (月) still hangs in the west — dawn: morning.
朝.mnemonic: Sun climbing through the reeds on the left, pale moon not yet gone on the right — あさ. Morning is the shift change, caught mid-handover.

lesson_examples.jp: 明日（あした）の　朝（あさ）まで　待（ま）って。
今朝（けさ）　無事（ぶじ）に　到着（とうちゃく）　しました。
lesson_examples.en: I arrived safe and sound this morning.

鳥.etymology: Pictograph: a long-tailed bird — crest, eye, folded wing, and the four dots of its tail feathers (灬).
鳥.mnemonic: Crest up, wing tucked, tail feathers fanned into four dots — とり. Remove one stroke (the eye) and the poor thing goes 烏, blind crow.

lesson_examples.jp: 鳥（とり）が　とんでいます。
小（ちい）さな　鳥（とり）の　こえが　します。
lesson_examples.en: I can hear a small bird.

meanings: counter for letters, notes, documents, etc.
通.etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 甬 'hollow tube' (phonetic ツウ) — passing through like water through a pipe: to go through, commute, connect.
通.mnemonic: The road becomes a tube and you slide through it, door to door, every day — とおる, かよう. 交通 is everyone in the tubes at once.

lesson_examples.jp: おっしゃる　通（とお）りです。
トムは　通（とお）りを　横切（よこぎ）った。

弟.etymology: Pictograph: a leather cord wound around a stake in descending turns — sequence, order of birth: the one born after, the younger brother.
弟.mnemonic: The cord spirals down the pole, turn below turn: he comes after you — おとうと. Birth order, drawn as a winding.

lesson_examples.jp: 弟（おとうと）は　ボストンに　住（す）んでいます。
lesson_examples.en: My brother is living in Boston.

lesson_examples.jp: 弟（おとうと）は　今（こん）　オーストラリアに　います。
lesson_examples.en: My brother is in Australia now.

冬.etymology: Compound: the tied-off ends of a rope (夂 — the year's thread finished) with ice (冫) beneath — the season that closes the year: winter.
冬.mnemonic: The year's rope tied off, two icicles hanging from the knot — ふゆ. Winter is the calendar's final knot, frozen stiff.

lesson_examples.jp: 冬休（ふゆやす）み　何日（なんにち）から？
lesson_examples.en: When does your winter vacation begin?

lesson_examples.jp: 冬休（ふゆやす）み　明（あ）けないで　ほしいな。
lesson_examples.en: I wish winter vacation would never end.

答.etymology: Phono-semantic: bamboo (竹) + 合 'fit' (phonetic トウ) — bamboo tally-slips split in two: the half that fits yours is the answer.
答.mnemonic: Snap the bamboo slip in two, keep one half: the reply that clicks (合) back into it is the answer — こたえ.

lesson_examples.jp: フランス語（ご）で　答（こた）えてください。
答（こた）えたくなかったら　答（こた）えなくていいからね。
lesson_examples.en: You don't have to answer if you don't want to.

頭.etymology: Phono-semantic: 豆 'ritual vessel on a stem' (phonetic トウ) + 頁 'head' — the head on its stem of a neck.
頭.mnemonic: A goblet (豆) balancing a big head (頁): don't tip it — あたま. When it aches, the vessel is overfull: 頭が痛い.

lesson_examples.jp: 頭（あたま）　痛（いた）い。
トムは　頭（あたま）が　いい。

同.etymology: Compound: one cover (the frame) over one (一) mouth (口) — many people speaking as one under one roof: same, together.
同.mnemonic: One hood, one line, one mouth: everyone inside says the same thing — おなじ. 同じ! echoes the room.

lesson_examples.jp: 心（こころ）から　同意（どうい）　します。
私（わたし）も　同（おな）じ　こと　考（かんが）え　てた。
lesson_examples.en: I was thinking the same thing.

肉.etymology: Pictograph: a slab of meat with its sinew-lines inside. As a component it disguises itself as 月 (the 'meat moon') in 体-adjacent kanji like 腹 and 脳.
肉.mnemonic: A cut of ribs hanging in the frame, marbling drawn as two little persons — にく. 焼肉: this kanji, grilling.

lesson_examples.jp: 肉（にく）が　すきです。
あの　みせの　肉（にく）は　おいしいです。
lesson_examples.en: The meat at that shop is good.

売.etymology: Simplified from 賣: taking out (出, worn into 士) what was bought (買, reduced to the cover and legs) — goods carried out to market: to sell.
売.mnemonic: A salesman (士) sets up his little stand (the cover) and runs (legs) after every customer — うる. 売り切れ: run after too well — sold out.

lesson_examples.jp: これ、売（う）り物（もの）ですか？
あの　店（みせ）で　ノートは　売（う）っていますか？
lesson_examples.en: Do they sell notebooks at that store?

風.etymology: Phono-semantic: a sail-canopy (凡, phonetic フウ) over an insect (虫) — the ancients believed wind bred the insects it carried: wind.
風.mnemonic: A sail bellies out and a single bug rides the gust inside it — かぜ. Wind carries seeds, smells, bugs and fashions: 和風, Japanese style, is Japan riding its own breeze.

lesson_examples.jp: きょうは　風（かぜ）が　つよいです。
あたたかい　風（かぜ）が　ふいて　います。

歩.etymology: Compound ideograph: two footprints, one after the other (止 + a reversed foot worn into 少) — left, right: to walk.
歩.mnemonic: Stop (止) a little (少), step, stop, step: that rhythm is walking — あるく. The 散歩 is the art of stopping slightly, beautifully.

lesson_examples.jp: 駅（えき）までは　歩（ある）いて　1時間（じかん）です。
lesson_examples.en: It takes you an hour to go to the station on foot.

lesson_examples.jp: 駅（えき）まで　一緒（いっしょ）に　歩（ある）きませんか？
lesson_examples.en: Let's walk to the station together.

方.etymology: Origin debated — a plow, or two boats lashed side by side. It has meant 'direction, side' since the oracle bones, and politely, 'the person over on that side'.
方.mnemonic: A weathervane with a crooked tail, pointing somewhere — ほう, the direction; かた, the honored person standing that way. あの方 = that way, that person.

lesson_examples.jp: 日本（にっぽん）の　方（ほう）ですか？
新入生（しんにゅうせい）の　方（ほう）ですか？

妹.etymology: Phono-semantic: woman (女) + 未 'not yet' (phonetic マイ) — the woman not yet grown: the younger sister.
妹.mnemonic: A girl (女) with a 'not yet' (未) pinned to her: not yet as tall as you, not yet allowed to stay up — いもうと.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　妹（いもうと）です。
これは　姉妹（しまい）です。

明.etymology: Compound ideograph: sun (日) and moon (月) shining together — the two lights of heaven in one character: bright, clear.
明.mnemonic: Sun and moon on at the same time: maximum brightness — あかるい. 明日 is the bright side of midnight: tomorrow.

lesson_examples.jp: また　明日（あした）。
明日（あした）は　日曜日（にちようび）です。

門.etymology: Pictograph: a double-leafed gate, both doors on their hinges. As a frame-component it hosts whatever happens at the threshold (間, 開, 聞).
門.mnemonic: Two saloon doors still swinging — モン. Whoever stands inside this frame in a kanji is doing something at the gate: listening (聞), opening (開), measuring the gap (間).

lesson_examples.jp: 門（もん）が　あります。
大（おお）きな　門（もん）の　まえで　まって　います。
lesson_examples.en: I'm waiting in front of the big gate.

夜.etymology: Phono-semantic: a person (亻) under a cover (亠) with the moon (夕) tucked at their side — the dark hours a person spends under shelter: night.
夜.mnemonic: Coat on the hook, someone home under the roof, the moon leaning at the window — よる. 今夜: tonight, the moon already in position.

lesson_examples.jp: 今夜（こんや）　トムに　会（あ）った。
明日（あした）の　夜（よる）とか　どう？

野.etymology: Phono-semantic: 里 'village and its fields' + 予 (phonetic ヤ) — the open land beyond the last houses: plains, the wild.
野.mnemonic: Past the village (里) the fences stop and the grass takes over — の. 野球 is baseball: the game of the open field.

lesson_examples.jp: 好（す）きな　野菜（やさい）は　何（なに）ですか？
野球（やきゅう）って　何（なに）が　面白（おもしろ）いの？

曜.etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 翟 'pheasant with spread feathers' (phonetic ヨウ) — the shining of the heavenly bodies, adopted to name the days of the week.
曜.mnemonic: The sun preening its feathered wings — a different plumage every day of the week: ヨウ. 月曜日, 火曜日… seven outfits, one bird.

lesson_examples.jp: 明日（あした）は　日曜日（にちようび）です。
今日（きょう）は　木曜日（もくようび）です。

用.etymology: Pictograph of debated origin — a bucket or a section of fencing. It has meant 'use, employ, task' since the earliest inscriptions.
用.mnemonic: A sturdy bucket ribbed with slats: grabbed every single day because it just works — もちいる, ヨウ. 用事 is whatever the bucket is needed for today.

lesson_examples.jp: 明日（あした）は　用事（ようじ）が　あります。
lesson_examples.en: I have things to do tomorrow.

lesson_examples.jp: こちらの　用紙（ようし）に　記入（きにゅう）　してください。

理.etymology: Phono-semantic: jade (王) + 里 (phonetic リ) — carving jade along its natural veins: the inner pattern of things, hence reason, logic.
理.mnemonic: Cut the gem with its grain, never against: follow the hidden lines — リ. 料理, 理由, 無理 — cooking, reasons, and what goes against the grain.

lesson_examples.jp: 無理（むり）　しないでね。
理由（りゆう）　聞（き）いても　いい？

羽.etymology: Pictograph: a pair of wings, each with its barbs — feathers; the counter for birds and rabbits.
羽.mnemonic: Two wings folded side by side — はね. Rabbits get counted with it too: monks once declared them 'birds' to eat them.

lesson_examples.jp: とりの　羽（はね）です。
これは　羽田（はねだ）です。

雲.etymology: 云 alone was the original cloud pictograph — curling vapor; the rain crown (雨) was added once 云 got borrowed for 'to say'.
雲.mnemonic: Vapor curling up (云) until the sky's ceiling (雨) catches it — くも. A cloud is rain still making up its mind.

lesson_examples.jp: 今日（きょう）の　空（そら）は　雲（くも）に　覆（おお）われている。
lesson_examples.en: The sky is covered with clouds today.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　雲（くも）をつかむようです。

園.etymology: Phono-semantic: walls (囗) + 袁 (phonetic エン) — a walled pleasure-ground: garden, park.
園.mnemonic: Trailing robes strolling inside the walls: the palace garden — その, エン. 公園 opened those walls to everyone; 動物園 filled them with animals.

lesson_examples.jp: ここは　わたしの　園（その）です。
これは　幼稚園（ようちえん）です。

黄.etymology: Origin debated — most read the old form as a person wearing a great jade pendant at the belt; it has meant 'yellow' since the oracle bones.
黄.mnemonic: A courtier weighed down by an amber pendant, glowing at the waist — きいろ. Yellow is the color of worn treasure.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　黄色（きいろ）いです。
これは　黄（き）です。

科.etymology: Compound ideograph: grain (禾) sorted with the measuring ladle (斗) — grading into kinds: category, department, branch of study.
科.mnemonic: Scoop the harvest into bins: this grade here, that grade there — カ. 科学 sorts the world; 歯科 is the tooth bin.

lesson_examples.jp: りか の　科目（かもく）が　すきです。
これは　科学（かがく）です。

絵.etymology: Simplified from 繪: threads (糸) brought together (会) — colored silks meeting in embroidery: a picture.
絵.mnemonic: Where the colored threads all meet (会), an image appears — え. Before paint, pictures were sewn.

lesson_examples.jp: この　絵（え）を　描（えが）いた　のは　誰（だれ）ですか？
これは　絵（え）です。

角.etymology: Pictograph: an animal horn with its striations — a horn; hence anything that juts: angle, corner.
角.mnemonic: A striped horn planted point-up — つの; turn at it and it's the かど, the street corner; measure it and it's カク, the angle.

lesson_examples.jp: そこの　角（かど）です。
これは　角度（かくど）です。

活.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + a phonetic written 舌 — water rushing and gurgling: alive, vigorous.
活.mnemonic: A stream chattering like a tongue (舌): that sound is aliveness — カツ. 生活 is your daily portion of it.

lesson_examples.jp: ドイツでの　生活（せいかつ）は　どう？
これは　活気（かっき）です。

丸.etymology: Pictograph: a person curled into a ball mid-tumble — round, whole.
丸.mnemonic: Knees to chin, rolling downhill — まる. Ships and castle keeps take it as a name-ending: the 〜丸, snug and complete.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　丸（まる）める。
これは　丸々（まるまる）です。

岩.etymology: Compound ideograph: mountain (山) + stone (石) — mountain-sized stone: a boulder, bedrock.
岩.mnemonic: A stone with a whole mountain stacked on top — いわ. Not a pebble: the kind climbers rope onto.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　岩（いわ）です。
岩（いわ）が　すきです。

記.etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 己 (phonetic キ) — words set down so the self won't forget: to record.
記.mnemonic: Write it down (言) for your future self (己) — キ. 日記 is that deal kept nightly; the 記者 keeps it for everyone.

lesson_examples.jp: こちらの　用紙（ようし）に　記入（きにゅう）　してください。
まいにち　記（しる）す。

形.etymology: Phono-semantic: 开 'frame' (phonetic ケイ) + 彡 'strokes of shading' — the outline plus its rendering: shape, form.
形.mnemonic: First the frame, then three quick shading strokes: the form appears — かたち. Every 人形 (doll) is born this way.

lesson_examples.jp: この　文（ぶん）は　現在（げんざい）　形（かたち）です。
lesson_examples.en: This sentence is in the present tense.

lesson_examples.jp: この　文（ぶん）の　時制（じせい）は　現在（げんざい）　形（かたち）です。
lesson_examples.en: This sentence is in the present tense.

原.etymology: Compound ideograph: a spring (泉) welling at the foot of a cliff (厂) — the source; and the open land it waters: plain, meadow; hence 'original'.
原.mnemonic: Where the water first leaves the rock: the source — はら, the open field it feeds; ゲン, the origin of things (原因).

lesson_examples.jp: 映画（えいが）　観（み）る　前（まえ）に　原作（げんさく）　読（よ）ん　どけばよかった。
lesson_examples.en: I should've read the original work before watching the movie.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　原則（げんそく）です。

戸.etymology: Pictograph: a single door leaf on its hinge — half of the double gate 門: the household door, and the counter for households.
戸.mnemonic: One door leaf, slightly ajar — と. A 門 is for the city; a 戸 is for your house. 江戸: the door of the bay.

lesson_examples.jp: 戸（と）を　あけます。
これは　井戸（いど）です。

交.etymology: Pictograph: a person standing with legs crossed — crossing, exchanging, mingling.
交.mnemonic: Legs crossed mid-dance-step: paths crossing everywhere — まじわる. 交通 is a whole city doing it at once.

lesson_examples.jp: 次（つぎ）の　交差点（こうさてん）を　右（みぎ）に　曲（ま）がってください。
lesson_examples.en: Turn right at the next intersection.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　交（か）わす。
