公.etymology: Compound ideograph, by the classic account: to divide (八) away the private (厶) — what belongs to no one alone: public.
公.mnemonic: Split open the private pocket and share it out: public property — コウ. The 公園 is the garden nobody owns and everybody has.

lesson_examples.jp: そんな　の　不公平（ふこうへい）じゃない？
これは　公私（こうし）です。

才.etymology: Pictograph read as a new sprout breaking the ground — raw, inborn capacity: talent; borrowed in Japanese as the everyday counter for age.
才.mnemonic: One shoot up before the field is even plowed: born gifted — サイ. Age borrowed the character: 十才, ten years grown.

lesson_examples.jp: トムくんは　7才（さい）、メアリーさんは　11才（さい）です。　トムくんが　メアリーさんより　年上（としうえ）に　なる　のは　何年後（なんねんご）でしょうか。
lesson_examples.en: Tom is seven, Mary is eleven. How many years will it be until Tom becomes older than Mary?

lesson_examples.jp: これは　才能（さいのう）です。

細.etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + a right side originally the fontanelle 囟 (later written 田) — thread fine as a baby's hair: thin, detailed.
細.mnemonic: Thread split until it's almost thought — ほそい. 細かい is that fineness applied to details (and to people who mind them).

lesson_examples.jp: そんな　細（こま）かい　こと　どうでも　いいじゃん。
lesson_examples.en: You shouldn't worry about something so small.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　細工（さいく）です。

算.etymology: Compound ideograph: hands (廾) working bamboo counting-rods (竹) on the board — to calculate.
算.mnemonic: Bamboo rods clicking between busy hands: ancient spreadsheet — サン. 計算 still means moving the rods, just faster.

lesson_examples.jp: 計算（けいさん）を　します。
これは　換算（かんさん）です。

寺.etymology: Originally 'to hold, administer' (a foot + a hand): a government office; when Buddhism arrived, the office that housed foreign monks became the temple.
寺.mnemonic: The old administration building handed over to the monks — てら. It still administrates: bells, time, and half the kanji it appears in (時, 待, 持).

lesson_examples.jp: 山（やま）の　上（うえ）の　寺（てら）に　のぼります。
lesson_examples.en: We climb to the temple on the mountain.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　寺（てら）です。

数.etymology: Simplified from 數: a hand with a stick (攵) tallying off a bundled phonetic — to count; a number.
数.mnemonic: Tap, tap, tap — the stick counts the sacks of rice — かず, スウ. 数学 is the tapping turned into a science.

lesson_examples.jp: 手数料（てすうりょう）は　いくらですか。
数学（すうがく）の　テスト　どうだった？

星.etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 生 (phonetic セイ) — lights born (生) of the same fire as the sun, scattered small: stars.
星.mnemonic: Baby suns sprouting (生) across the night field — ほし. Each star is the sun's seedling.

lesson_examples.jp: 星（ほし）が　きれいな　よるです。
これは　惑星（わくせい）です。

晴.etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 青 'blue' (phonetic セイ) — the sun in a blue sky: clear weather.
晴.mnemonic: Sun plus blue: the forecast you wanted — はれ. 晴れ is the sky wearing its best kanji.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　素晴（すば）らしい。
ボストンは　素晴（すば）らしい　街（まち）です。

雪.etymology: Compound ideograph: rain (雨) + a hand with a broom (彗 reduced to ヨ) — the one precipitation you have to sweep: snow.
雪.mnemonic: Rain you shovel — ゆき. The broom under the rain-crown is the whole story of a northern winter.

lesson_examples.jp: あ、雪（ゆき）だ！
外（そと）は　雪（ゆき）だよ。

線.etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 泉 'spring' (phonetic セン) — a thread flowing continuous as spring-water: a line.
線.mnemonic: Water from the spring pulled into a thread that never breaks — セン. Train lines (山手線), phone lines, pencil lines: all this thread.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　路線（ろせん）です。
これは　沿線（えんせん）です。

船.etymology: Phono-semantic: boat (舟) + 㕣 (phonetic セン) — the full-sized vessel: a ship.
船.mnemonic: The little boat (舟) that grew a cabin and a cargo hold — ふね. 風船 is its airborne cousin: a balloon, ship of wind.

lesson_examples.jp: 船（ふね）で　しまへ　わたります。
lesson_examples.en: We cross to the island by boat.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　船（ふね）です。

組.etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 且 (phonetic ソ) — cords braided together: to assemble; the group so woven.
組.mnemonic: Strands braided into one rope: the team — くみ. 組み立てる is braiding parts into a machine; a 番組 braids minutes into a show.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　仕組（しく）みです。
まいにち　組（く）む。

谷.etymology: Pictograph: slopes parting above a mouth-like opening — the cleft where water exits the mountains: a valley.
谷.mnemonic: Two ridges peel apart and the land opens its mouth — たに. 渋谷: the valley that got a scramble crossing.

lesson_examples.jp: ふかい　谷（たに）です。
これは　谷（たに）です。

直.etymology: Compound ideograph: ten (十) eyes (目) inspecting even the hidden corner (乚) — nothing crooked survives: straight, honest; to set straight.
直.mnemonic: Ten eyes check the corner and the line comes out true — なおす, to fix; ただちに, straight away. Honesty is just geometry with witnesses.

lesson_examples.jp: 今（いま）から　直（なお）します。
私（わたし）が　直接（ちょくせつ）　お　伺（うかが）い　します。

点.etymology: Simplified from 點 'black mark': 占 (phonetic テン) over fire (灬) — a burn-black dot: a point, a mark, a score.
点.mnemonic: The fortune-teller (占) drops sparks (灬) — each scorch mark one point — テン. Tests are scored in little burns: 百点!

lesson_examples.jp: 気温（きおん）は　氷点下（ひょうてんか）　6度（ど）です。
次（つぎ）の　交差点（こうさてん）を　右（みぎ）に　曲（ま）がってください。
lesson_examples.en: Turn right at the next intersection.

当.etymology: Simplified from 當: 尚 (phonetic トウ) over 田 — fields matched in value: fitting exactly; hence to hit the mark, to be right.
当.mnemonic: The dart lands dead on — あたる. 当たり! for the winning ticket; 本当 for the statement that hits reality square.

lesson_examples.jp: 本当（ほんとう）に　ありがとう。
これは　本当（ほんとう）の　話（はなし）です。

内.etymology: Compound ideograph: entering (入) under a cover (冂) — what is within: inside.
内.mnemonic: Step in under the tent flap: now you're in-house — うち. 家内, 案内, 内緒: family, guidance, secrets — all indoor matters.

lesson_examples.jp: トムには　絶対（ぜったい）　内緒（ないしょ）だよ。
lesson_examples.en: No matter what, don't tell Tom.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　身内（みうち）です。

馬.etymology: Pictograph: a horse — arched neck with mane (the top strokes) and four galloping legs flattened into dots (灬).
馬.mnemonic: Mane flying, four hooves drumming into dots — うま. Stations (駅) and tests (験) still carry this horse inside them.

lesson_examples.jp: 男子（だんし）って　みんな　馬鹿（ばか）だよね。
なんで　そんな　馬鹿（ばか）な　こと　したの？
lesson_examples.en: Why did you do something stupid like that?

麦.etymology: Simplified from 麥: the wheat plant (來) with a foot (夂) below — grain trodden into the winter field: barley, wheat.
麦.mnemonic: Stamp the seed in and let winter do the rest — むぎ. Beer, udon and bread all start at this footprint.

lesson_examples.jp: 麦（むぎ）を　そだてます。
これは　蕎麦（そば）です。

番.etymology: Compound ideograph: an animal's paw-print (釆) crossing a field (田) — tracks in sequence: one's turn, a number in a series.
番.mnemonic: Prints across the paddy, one after another: whose turn is it? — バン. 一番 is the first footprint; 電話番号 a whole trail of them.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　クラスで　一番（いちばん）だ。
lesson_examples.en: Tom is first in his class.

lesson_examples.jp: 一番（いちばん）の　違（ちが）いは　何（なに）ですか？

米.etymology: Pictograph: rice grains spreading from the ear of the plant. Also abbreviates アメリカ (米国) by old phonetic convention.
米.mnemonic: Six grains bursting off the stalk — こめ. One kanji feeds a continent and names another: 米国, the rice-character country that grows wheat.

lesson_examples.jp: お米（こめ）を　たべます。
これは　米（こめ）です。

鳴.etymology: Compound ideograph: mouth (口) + bird (鳥) — the bird's voice: to cry, chirp; of things, to ring and sound.
鳴.mnemonic: Give the bird its mouth back and the morning starts — なく. Phones, bells and stomachs all 鳴る: everything chirps in Japanese.

lesson_examples.jp: キリンってなんて　鳴（な）く　んだろう？
まいにち　鳴（な）く。

毛.etymology: Pictograph: a tuft of hair curling at the tip — fur, hair, down.
毛.mnemonic: One curling hair, magnified — け. 毛布 is a blanket of it; the 髪の毛 on your head is this kanji by the hundred thousand.

lesson_examples.jp: この　ねこは　毛（け）が　ながいです。
これは　睫毛（まつげ）です。

汽.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 气 'breath' (phonetic キ) — water become breath: steam.
汽.mnemonic: Water exhaling — キ. 汽車: the train that ran on sighs.

lesson_examples.jp: 汽車（きしゃ）が　走（はし）ります。
これは　汽車（きしゃ）です。

弓.etymology: Pictograph: an unstrung bow in profile.
弓.mnemonic: The curve waiting for its string — ゆみ. It arms 引, 強, 弱 across the dictionary.

lesson_examples.jp: 弓（ゆみ）の　練習（れんしゅう）を　します。
これは　弓（ゆみ）です。

刀.etymology: Pictograph: a single-edged blade with its curved back. As a right-side component it sharpens into 刂.
刀.mnemonic: The katana's silhouette in two strokes — かたな. 日本刀: the pictograph, forged.

lesson_examples.jp: 古（ふる）い　刀（かたな）を　見（み）ました。
これは　刀（かたな）です。

矢.etymology: Pictograph: an arrow — head at the top, fletching below.
矢.mnemonic: Nocked and ready — や. Inside 知 it's the answer in flight.

lesson_examples.jp: 矢（や）で　まとを　いました。
lesson_examples.en: I shot the target with an arrow.

lesson_examples.jp: かんばんに　矢印（やじるし）が　あります。
lesson_examples.en: There's an arrow on the sign.

里.etymology: Compound ideograph: fields (田) on tilled earth (土) — a settlement and the old league measuring the walk between them.
里.mnemonic: Field plus soil equals home village — さと. ふるさと的距離: measured in 里.

lesson_examples.jp: ふる里（さと）に　てがみを　かく。
lesson_examples.en: I write home to my birthplace.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　里（さと）です。

安.etymology: Compound ideograph: a woman (女) at rest under a roof (宀) — peace, safety, ease. 'Cheap' grew later from 'easy on the purse'.
安.mnemonic: Home at last, under her own roof, she finally relaxes — やすい. And relax your wallet too: this shop is 安い, reassuringly cheap.

lesson_examples.jp: それ　聞（き）いて　安心（あんしん）　したよ。
もう少（すこ）し　安（やす）く　なりませんか。
lesson_examples.en: Can you give me a discount?

飲.etymology: Compound: the food vessel (飠) + 欠, a person with mouth stretched wide open — head tipped back, pouring it down: to drink.
飲.mnemonic: Head thrown back (欠) over the covered jar (飠): glug, glug — のむ. 飲み物 is anything that disappears that way.

lesson_examples.jp: お　酒（さけ）は　飲（の）まれますか？
何（なに）か　お　飲（の）みに　なりますか？
lesson_examples.en: Would you like something to drink?

駅.etymology: Simplified from 驛: horse (馬) + a phonetic (originally 睪, trimmed to 尺). The relay post of the imperial roads, where riders changed horses — reborn as the railway station.
駅.mnemonic: Where travelers once measured out (尺) a fresh horse (馬), they now measure out a train — えき. Same spot on the map, two thousand years apart: 駅前 is still the busiest corner in town.

lesson_examples.jp: 駅（えき）まで　一緒（いっしょ）に　行（い）かない？
lesson_examples.en: Do you want to go to the station with me?

lesson_examples.jp: 映画館（えいがかん）は　駅（えき）から　近（ちか）いの？
lesson_examples.en: Is the movie theater near the station?

悪.etymology: Phono-semantic: 亜 — the cramped floor-plan of an ancient tomb chamber (phonetic ア) — + heart (心): a heart twisted into a cramped shape: bad, evil.
悪.mnemonic: A heart squeezed into a tomb-shaped box until it warps — わるい. Villains aren't born; their 心 just ran out of floor space.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　目（め）が　悪（わる）い。
発音（はつおん）　悪（わる）くて　ごめん。
lesson_examples.en: I'm sorry my pronunciation isn't very good.

暗.etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 音 (phonetic アン) — the sun muffled like a sound behind a wall: dark, dim; also 'by heart' (in the dark, without looking).
暗.mnemonic: The lights go out and the sun becomes a sound you can only hear — くらい. 暗記: learning in the dark, eyes closed.

lesson_examples.jp: そんな　暗（くら）い　ところで　何（なに）　し　てるの？
lesson_examples.en: What are you doing in a dark place like that?

lesson_examples.jp: これは　暗唱（あんしょう）です。

意.etymology: Compound ideograph: the sound (音) of the heart (心) — what the heart is saying before the mouth does: intention, meaning, idea.
意.mnemonic: Put a stethoscope to the chest: the heart is humming a plan — イ. 意味 is the meaning; 注意 is turning the volume up on it.

lesson_examples.jp: どういう　意味（いみ）？
心（こころ）から　同意（どうい）　します。

医.etymology: Simplified from 醫: an arrow (矢) in a surgeon's box (匚) — the healer who pulls arrowheads from wounds: doctor.
医.mnemonic: Open the doctor's case: inside, the arrow he just removed — イ. The 医者 keeps every arrow life fires at you.

lesson_examples.jp: わたしの　ちちは　医者（いしゃ）です。
しょうらい、医者（いしゃ）に　なりたいです。
lesson_examples.en: I want to become a doctor in the future.

員.etymology: Originally the round mouth (口) of a bronze tripod vessel (貝-shaped below) — 'round' was borrowed long ago for counting people: member, personnel.
員.mnemonic: A mouth to feed sitting on the payroll money (貝): one head counted — イン. 店員, 会社員, 駅員: wherever there's a counter, there's an 員 behind it.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　委員（いいん）です。
これは　従業員（じゅうぎょういん）です。

院.etymology: Phono-semantic: wall/mound (阝) + 完 'complete' (phonetic イン) — a compound completely enclosed by walls: an institution.
院.mnemonic: Walls (阝) all the way around until the enclosure is complete (完): hospital, temple, academy — イン. 病院: the walled place you'd rather visit than inhabit.

lesson_examples.jp: ここは　病院（びょういん）です。
顔色（かおいろ）　悪（わる）いけど　大丈夫（だいじょうぶ）？ 　病院（びょういん）　行（い）った　方（ほう）が　いい　んじゃない？
lesson_examples.en: Your face looks pale. Are you OK? Maybe it would be better if you went to the hospital, don't you think?

運.etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 軍 'army' (phonetic ウン) — army wagons rolling supplies down the road: to transport; and the fortune that rolls with the convoy.
運.mnemonic: The supply wagons roll: whatever they bring you is your luck — はこぶ, ウン. 運転 is keeping your own wagon on the road; 運がいい is when the road is kind.

lesson_examples.jp: トムって　運（うん）が　いいよね。
久（ひさ）しぶりに　運動（うんどう）　したから　めっちゃ　疲（つか）れた。
lesson_examples.en: I exercised like I used to, and now I'm all worn out.

屋.etymology: Compound: a low covering (尸) over 至 'arrive' — the shelter you arrive under: roof, house; in Japanese, the shop and its keeper (〜屋).
屋.mnemonic: Duck under the low roof: you've arrived at the shop — や. 本屋, パン屋, 花屋 — every trade gets its own little roof.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　屋根（やね）の　上（うえ）に　いる。
トムって　気分屋（きぶんや）だよね。

界.etymology: Phono-semantic: field (田) + 介 'between' (phonetic カイ) — the dividing ridges between fields: boundaries, and the bounded whole they define — the world.
界.mnemonic: Stand on the ridge between two paddies: every world is fields plus fences — カイ. 世界: all the fields, all the fences, seen at once.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　他界（たかい）です。
これは　世界中（せかいじゅう）です。

開.etymology: Compound ideograph: two hands (开) lifting the bar from inside the gate (門) — to open.
開.mnemonic: Both hands on the crossbar, lift, and the gate swings — あける, ひらく. The elevator button says 開: hands off the bar, doors open.

lesson_examples.jp: かばん　開（ひら）いてますよ。
窓（まど）を　開（あ）けてください。

寒.etymology: Compound ideograph: a person packed in straw under a roof, ice (冫) at the bottom — winter insulation, ancient style: cold.
寒.mnemonic: Stuffed under the blankets, hay in the walls, and still two icicles at your feet — さむい. Cold enough that even the kanji is bundled up.

lesson_examples.jp: ちょっと　寒（さむ）くないですか？
半袖（はんそで）で　寒（さむ）くない　んですか？
lesson_examples.en: Aren't you cold in short sleeves?

漢.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + a phonetic — the Han River, which named the Han dynasty, which named the Chinese script itself: 漢字.
漢.mnemonic: A river (氵) so important a dynasty took its name, and the dynasty named the characters — カン. Every 漢字 you learn flows out of that one river.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　漢（かん）の　じだいです。
これは　漢字（かんじ）です。

館.etymology: Phono-semantic: food (飠) + 官 'official' (phonetic カン) — the official guesthouse where envoys were fed: a grand building, a hall.
館.mnemonic: The building big enough to feed officials — カン. Libraries (図書館), cinemas (映画館), embassies (大使館): if it has marble floors, it ends in 館.

lesson_examples.jp: 映画館（えいがかん）は　駅（えき）から　近（ちか）いの？
lesson_examples.en: Is the movie theater near the station?

lesson_examples.jp: オランダ　大使館（たいしかん）は　どこですか？

起.etymology: Phono-semantic: run (走) + 己 'self' (phonetic キ) — the self getting up and breaking into a run: to rise, to wake, to start.
起.mnemonic: The alarm rings and your self (己) launches into a sprint (走) — おきる. Every day 起きる is the first race you win or lose.

lesson_examples.jp: まだ　起（お）き　てる？
何（なに）が　起（お）こった　のですか。

急.etymology: Compound: a hand reaching to catch someone ahead (an old form of 及) over a heart (心) — the heart straining to catch up: hurry, urgent.
急.mnemonic: Your hand grabs for the closing train door and your heart slams — いそぐ. 急行: the train for hearts in exactly that state.

lesson_examples.jp: 急（いそ）いで！
お　急（いそ）ぎですか？

究.etymology: Phono-semantic: hole (穴) + 九 (phonetic キュウ) — probing a cave to its very last turn: to investigate exhaustively.
究.mnemonic: Crawl into the cave (穴) nine (九) turns deep, to the very end — キュウ. 研究 is refusing to stop at turn eight.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　究明（きゅうめい）です。
これは　追究（ついきゅう）です。

去.etymology: Compound ideograph: a figure striding away from a hollow or dwelling (厶) — departed: gone; of time, the past.
去.mnemonic: Footsteps walking away from the empty nest — さる. 去年 is the year that walked off and isn't coming back.

lesson_examples.jp: 去年（きょねん）の　クリスマスは　何（なに）　し　てた？
lesson_examples.en: What did you do last Christmas?

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　去（さ）る。

業.etymology: Pictograph: a notched wooden rack for hanging bells and drums — the equipment of one's craft: work, trade, vocation (and karma, in the temples).
業.mnemonic: Your tools hung on the rack in their notches: that rack is your trade — ギョウ. 卒業 is the day you hang them up at school for the last time.

lesson_examples.jp: 郵便局（ゆうびんきょく）の　営業（えいぎょう）　時間（じかん）は　何時（なんじ）からですか？
lesson_examples.en: When does the post office open?

lesson_examples.jp: 工業（こうぎょう）が　さかんな　まちです。
lesson_examples.en: It's a town where industry thrives.

銀.etymology: Phono-semantic: metal (金) + 艮 (phonetic ギン) — the metal that stands second to gold: silver.
銀.mnemonic: Gold's quieter sibling, same mine, one shade paler — ギン. Banks (銀行) are where silver goes to work; the Ginza is where it goes to shop.

lesson_examples.jp: ここから　一番（いちばん）　近（ちか）い　銀行（ぎんこう）は　どこですか？
これは　銀行（ぎんこう）です。

区.etymology: Simplified from 區: a box (匚) crowded with mouths/households (品, reduced to メ) — a district full of homes: a ward.
区.mnemonic: One drawer of the city's filing cabinet, an X marking your neighborhood — ク. 渋谷区, 新宿区: Tokyo is a cabinet of 23 drawers.

lesson_examples.jp: この　区（く）は　しずかです。
わたしは　この　区（く）に　すんで　います。

軽.etymology: Phono-semantic: cart (車) + 圣 (simplified 巠, phonetic ケイ) — a cart light enough to fly down the road: lightweight.
軽.mnemonic: A cart loaded with nothing but thread: the horse barely notices — かるい. 軽自動車: the modern featherweight cart.

lesson_examples.jp: ごめん、軽（かる）い　冗談（じょうだん）の　つもりだった　んだけど。
lesson_examples.en: Sorry, I only meant it as a joke.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　軽蔑（けいべつ）です。

研.etymology: Compound: stone (石) + 开 'made level/even' — grinding on a stone until flat and sharp: to polish; figuratively, to grind at a subject.
研.mnemonic: Blade on the whetstone, back and forth until it gleams level — と(ぐ). 研究: polishing a question until it cuts.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　研究（けんきゅう）です。
これは　研究者（けんきゅうしゃ）です。

県.etymology: Simplified from 縣, which grimly showed a head hung upside-down by a cord — the original sense was 'to suspend' (ancestor of 懸); borrowed for the administrative district 'suspended' from the capital.
県.mnemonic: A watchful eye (目) hanging from the capital by a thread: local government — ケン. All 43 県 dangle from Tokyo on the same string.

lesson_examples.jp: となりの　県（けん）に　いきます。
lesson_examples.en: I'm going to the next prefecture.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　県（けん）です。

仕.etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 士 'gentleman-retainer' (phonetic シ) — a person in service to a lord: to serve, to work.
仕.mnemonic: A person standing at the gentleman's side, ready — つかえる. 仕事 is the modern lord: service, five days a week.

lesson_examples.jp: 仕事（しごと）は　どうですか？
お　仕事（しごと）は　何（なに）を　され　てる　んですか？

使.etymology: Compound: person (亻) + 吏 'official' — a person dispatched on official business: an envoy; to employ, to use.
使.mnemonic: The boss points: you, go — you've been used, err, dispatched — つかう. The 大使 is the grandest errand-runner of all: the ambassador.

lesson_examples.jp: 何（なに）に　使（つか）うの？
パソコン　使（つか）っても　いい？

始.etymology: Phono-semantic: woman (女) + 台 (phonetic シ) — the ancients located every beginning in the mother: to begin.
始.mnemonic: Every story starts the same way: a woman (女) on the stage (台) — はじめる. 始めまして: 'we are at the beginning', the first greeting.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　もう　始（はじ）めている。
トムは　言（い）い訳（わけ）を　始（はじ）めた。

死.etymology: Compound ideograph: bare bones (歹) with a person kneeling beside them (匕) — the mourner at the remains: death.
死.mnemonic: Someone kneels by what is left — しぬ. The number four (シ) shares its sound, which is why hospitals skip the 4th floor.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　死（し）んだ？
笑（わら）い　すぎて　死（し）ぬかと　思（おも）った。
lesson_examples.en: I laughed so much, I thought I'd die.

事.etymology: Pictograph: a hand gripping a writing tablet or flagged pole — official business being recorded: an affair, a matter, the abstract 'thing'.
事.mnemonic: A clerk's hand skewering paperwork on a spike — こと. Intangible things only: 仕事 the work-thing, 食事 the meal-thing, 大事 the thing that matters.

lesson_examples.jp: 仕事（しごと）は　どうですか？
トムから　返事（へんじ）　来（き）た？

持.etymology: Phono-semantic: hand (扌) + 寺 'temple' (phonetic ジ) — the hand that grips and keeps: to hold, to possess.
持.mnemonic: Hold it the way a temple holds its relics: firmly, forever — もつ. 気持ち is what your heart is currently holding.

lesson_examples.jp: 今（こん）　携帯（けいたい）　持（も）っ　てる？
lesson_examples.en: Do you have a cell phone with you?

lesson_examples.jp: イヤ　ホン　持（も）っ　てる？

写.etymology: Simplified from 寫, originally 'to transfer things into a house' — transferring an image onto paper: to copy, to photograph.
写.mnemonic: Slip the sheet under the cover (冖) and trace what shows through (与) — うつす. 写真: reality, transferred and 'true'.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　その　写真（しゃしん）を　見（み）た。
写真（しゃしん）を　撮（と）っていただけませんか？
lesson_examples.en: Would you please take a picture?

者.etymology: Originally a picture of firewood boiling something (the root of 煮), borrowed since antiquity for 'the one who…' — the all-purpose person suffix.
者.mnemonic: An old-timer (耂) telling stories in the sun (日): 'the one who…' — もの, シャ. 医者, 学者, 記者 — name the deed and 者 names the doer.

lesson_examples.jp: 医者（いしゃ）を　呼（よ）んで下（くだ）さい。
これは　読者（どくしゃ）です。

主.etymology: Pictograph: an oil lamp with its flame (the dot) — the master of the house keeps the lamp burning: lord, chief, main.
主.mnemonic: One flame on the lampstand and the whole household orbits it — ぬし, シュ. The 主人 is whoever tends the flame; the 主 idea is the one lit brightest.

lesson_examples.jp: この　いえの　主（ぬし）は　だれですか。
lesson_examples.en: Who is the master of this house?

lesson_examples.jp: これは　亭主（ていしゅ）です。

終.etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 冬 'winter' (phonetic シュウ) — the year's thread wound up at winter: to end.
終.mnemonic: Wind the last of the thread as the first ice forms: done — おわる. 終電: the day's thread runs out at the station.

lesson_examples.jp: 終電（しゅうでん）は　何時（なんじ）ですか？
lesson_examples.en: When does the last train leave?

lesson_examples.jp: 急（いそ）がないと　終電（しゅうでん）　逃（のが）すよ。
lesson_examples.en: If you don't hurry, you'll miss the last train.

習.etymology: Compound ideograph: young wings (羽) over 白 (originally the sun/self) — a fledgling flapping day after day until flight comes: to learn by repetition.
習.mnemonic: Little wings beating over the nest every single morning — ならう. 練習, 復習: learning is just flapping, counted in days.

lesson_examples.jp: トムを　見習（みなら）い　なさい。
これは　風習（ふうしゅう）です。

集.etymology: Compound ideograph: a bird (隹) on a tree (木) — the old form had three birds: a flock settling at dusk: to gather.
集.mnemonic: One tree, and every bird in the valley lands on it at sunset — あつまる. 集合! and the flock assembles.

lesson_examples.jp: 集合（しゅうごう）　場所（ばしょ）は　どこですか？
これは　特集（とくしゅう）です。

住.etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 主 'the lamp of the master' (phonetic ジュウ) — the person beside the burning lamp: to dwell.
住.mnemonic: Where your lamp (主) burns, that's where you live — すむ. 住所 is the map coordinate of your flame.

lesson_examples.jp: トムの　住所（じゅうしょ）　知（し）っ　てる？
住所（じゅうしょ）を　教（おし）えてください。

重.etymology: Pictograph: a person bent under a heavy sack pressing toward the ground — heavy; and layers stacked one on another (かさねる).
重.mnemonic: The porter's silhouette compressed by the load, stroke stacked on stroke — おもい. Heavy things pile: 重ねる; important things weigh: 大事×重 = 重要.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　とても　重要（じゅうよう）な　ポイントです。
lesson_examples.en: This is an extremely important point.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　重（おも）んじる。

所.etymology: Phono-semantic: door (戸) + axe (斤, phonetic ショ) — where the axe rings by the doorway: the spot, the place.
所.mnemonic: You can find the woodcutter's house with your eyes closed: follow the axe sound to the door — ところ. 台所, 住所, 場所 — every 'where' ends here.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　台所（だいどころ）だよ。
トムの　住所（じゅうしょ）　知（し）っ　てる？

暑.etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 者 (phonetic ショ — whose own origin is 'boiling') — the sun boiling the air: sultry heat.
暑.mnemonic: The sun sets the kettle of the sky to boil — あつい. August in Japan: the 者 under the 日 is you, simmering.

lesson_examples.jp: 暑（あつ）くないの？
今日（きょう）は　暑（あつ）いですね。

乗.etymology: Simplified from 乘: a person standing high in a tree, feet on the branches — climbing aboard: to ride, to mount.
乗.mnemonic: Climb the trunk, settle on the highest branch: all aboard — のる. Same move at the station every morning: 電車に乗る.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　車（くるま）に　乗（の）った。
この　バスは　50人乗（にんの）りです。
lesson_examples.en: This bus can hold fifty people.

真.etymology: Simplified from 眞: a filled vessel set perfectly upright — full to the brim, not a drop false: genuine, true.
真.mnemonic: Ten (十) eyes (目) inspected it on one (一) bench: certified true — まこと, シン. 写真 is 'the true copy'; 真ん中 the true middle.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　その　写真（しゃしん）を　見（み）た。
どう　したの？ 　顔（かお）　真（ま）っ青（さお）だよ。

進.etymology: Compound ideograph: movement (辶) + bird (隹) — birds cannot fly backward: to advance, only forward.
進.mnemonic: A bird on the road has one gear: forward — すすむ. When you can't reverse, every step is 前進.

lesson_examples.jp: 前（まえ）に　進（すす）んでください。
これは　進度（しんど）です。

世.etymology: Ideograph: three tens (十) joined at the base — thirty years: the span of one generation; then the world that generation inhabits.
世.mnemonic: Thirty years welded into one bracket: your allotted lap — よ, セ. 世界 is all the laps being run at once; お世話 is helping someone through theirs.

lesson_examples.jp: この　世（よ）は　ひろいです。
あたらしい　世（よ）が　はじまります。

送.etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + a phonetic showing hands lifting an offering — walking a gift or a guest on their way: to send, to see off.
送.mnemonic: Carry the parcel down the road with both hands until the road takes over — おくる. 見送り is when it's a person, and you wave until the train is gone.

lesson_examples.jp: 絶賛（ぜっさん）　放送中（ほうそうちゅう）！
これは　回送（かいそう）です。

族.etymology: Compound ideograph: a banner with an arrow beneath it — the clan mustered under its standard, arrows ready: tribe, family line.
族.mnemonic: One flag, everyone's arrows stacked beneath it: that's a family — ゾク. 家族: the tribe whose banner hangs at your door.

lesson_examples.jp: うちは　4人（にん）　家族（かぞく）です。
lesson_examples.en: There are four people in my family.

lesson_examples.jp: わが家（や）は　4人（にん）　家族（かぞく）です。
lesson_examples.en: There are four people in my family.

待.etymology: Phono-semantic: step (彳) + 寺 'temple' (phonetic タイ) — pacing back and forth before the temple where you were told to be: to wait.
待.mnemonic: Little steps in front of the temple gate, checking the road again — まつ. ちょっと待って: two more paces, they'll come.

lesson_examples.jp: 誰（だれ）　待（ま）っ　てるの？
待（ま）たせて　ごめん。
lesson_examples.en: Sorry to have kept you waiting.

meanings: counter for decades of ages, eras, etc.
代.etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 弋 'stake, tally' (phonetic ダイ) — one person staked in for another: substitute; the tally of reigns: era; the tally of payment: fee.
代.mnemonic: Plant a stake where you stood and someone takes your shift — かわる. Eras substitute for eras (時代), coins for goods (電気代): the same swap, three sizes.

lesson_examples.jp: 大学（だいがく）　時代（じだい）の　専攻（せんこう）は　何（なに）でしたか？
lesson_examples.en: What did you major in at college?

lesson_examples.jp: パンの　お　代（か）わりは　いかがですか？
lesson_examples.en: Would you like some more bread?

題.etymology: Phono-semantic: 是 (phonetic ダイ) + 頁 'head' — what stands at the head of a text: its title, its topic.
題.mnemonic: The heading at the top of the page, big letters, first thing your head meets — ダイ. 宿題 is the topic that follows you home; 問題 the one that fights back.

lesson_examples.jp: 問題（もんだい）を　再（さい）　検討（けんとう）　してみます。
すみません、宿題（しゅくだい）　忘（わす）れました。
lesson_examples.en: I'm sorry, I forgot to do my homework.

短.etymology: Compound: arrow (矢) + 豆 'stemmed vessel' — the ancients measured small lengths against arrows and cups: short.
短.mnemonic: Measured against a single arrow, it doesn't even reach the cup: short — みじかい. 短い夏: a summer one arrow long.

lesson_examples.jp: この　えんぴつは　短（みじか）いです。
じかんが　短（みじか）いので、いそぎましょう。
lesson_examples.en: Time is short, so let's hurry.

着.etymology: Variant of 著 'to attach': clothing attached to the body — to wear; a traveler attached to the destination — to arrive.
着.mnemonic: Pull the wool sweater down past your eye (目): it's on — きる. The same 'sticking' gets the train to the platform: 到着.

lesson_examples.jp: 着（つ）いて来（こ）ないでよ。
トムは　最後（さいご）に　到着（とうちゃく）　した。

注.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 主 (phonetic チュウ) — water poured in a steady stream; attention poured onto a point.
注.mnemonic: The master (主) tips the jug and the water threads down in one line — そそぐ. 注意: pour your mind the same way, without splashing.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　注文（ちゅうもん）と　違（ちが）います。
lesson_examples.en: This is not what I ordered.

lesson_examples.jp: ご　注文（ちゅうもん）は　お決（き）まりですか？

転.etymology: Phono-semantic (simplified from 轉): cart (車) + 云 (from the phonetic 專) — wheels going around: to revolve, roll, tumble.
転.mnemonic: Cartwheels spinning till the spokes blur into clouds (云) — ころぶ, テン. 運転 is keeping the spin on the road; 自転車 is the spin you pedal.

lesson_examples.jp: 転（ころ）ばない　ようにね。
この　自転車（じてんしゃ）、誰（だれ）の？

都.etymology: Phono-semantic: 者 (phonetic ト) + city wall (阝) — the city of cities, seat of the court: the metropolis. 東京都 wears it today.
都.mnemonic: Everyone (者) plus walls: the city everybody moved to — みやこ, ト. 都合 is metropolitan scheduling: 'when the big city of my life allows'.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　都市（とし）です。
これは　都合（つごう）です。

度.etymology: Compound: under a roof (广), a hand (又) measuring in spans — a unit of measure: degree, and each 'take' of an action: once, twice.
度.mnemonic: A hand ticking off spans on the workshop wall: one notch, one degree, one time — ド. 今度 is 'this next notch'; 温度 the notches of heat.

lesson_examples.jp: 気温（きおん）は　氷点下（ひょうてんか）　6度（ど）です。
もう一度（いちど）　やってください。

動.etymology: Phono-semantic: 重 'heavy' (phonetic ドウ) + 力 'strength' — muscle set against a heavy load until it shifts: to move.
動.mnemonic: Put strength (力) against the heaviest sack (重) and it finally budges — うごく. 動物 are 'the moving things'; 自動 is the sack moving itself.

lesson_examples.jp: 動（うご）かないでください。
好（す）きな　動物（どうぶつ）は　何（なに）ですか？

発.etymology: Simplified from 發: feet planted apart (癶) and a bow releasing — the arrow leaves: to discharge, depart, emit.
発.mnemonic: Stance set, string loosed: whatever it was, it's launched — ハツ. Trains 出発, ideas 発明, words 発音 — all arrows off this one bow.

lesson_examples.jp: 発音（はつおん）　悪（わる）くて　ごめん。
lesson_examples.en: I'm sorry my pronunciation isn't very good.

lesson_examples.jp: 明日（あした）の　ご　出発（しゅっぱつ）は　何時（なんじ）ですか？
lesson_examples.en: What time do you leave tomorrow?

病.etymology: Phono-semantic: the sickbed radical (疒 — a person laid on a slanted cot) + 丙 (phonetic ビョウ/ヘイ): laid up: illness.
病.mnemonic: Flat on the tilted cot with a C-grade (丙) fever chart — びょうき. Everything under the 疒 roof is some way of feeling awful; 病院 is where the cots line up.

lesson_examples.jp: ここは　病院（びょういん）です。
トムは　病気（びょうき）なの？

品.etymology: Compound ideograph: three boxes/mouths stacked — wares piled for inspection; many mouths judging them gives 'quality, refinement'.
品.mnemonic: Three crates stacked in the shop window — しな. 品物 are the crates; 上品 is how neatly they're stacked.

lesson_examples.jp: この　お店（みせ）は　品（しな）ものが　おおい。
これは　品種（ひんしゅ）です。

服.etymology: Originally 'to make submit / to attach to one's service' (a hand pressing a kneeling figure); clothing is what attaches to the body — dress, and 'a dose' of tea or medicine.
服.mnemonic: The body (月) fitted into its uniform until it behaves — フク. 洋服, 制服: cloth that tells the flesh who's in charge today.

lesson_examples.jp: ちょっと　一服（いっぷく）　しませんか？
lesson_examples.en: What do you say to taking a rest?

lesson_examples.jp: 風邪（かぜ）　引（ひ）くから　早（はや）く　服（ふく）　着（き）　なさい。
lesson_examples.en: Put some clothes on, you'll catch a cold.

物.etymology: Phono-semantic: ox (牛) + 勿 'streamers of many colors' (phonetic ブツ/モツ) — oxen of every color: things of every kind, the physical 'thing'.
物.mnemonic: A cow walking through fluttering ribbons: cargo of every color — もの. 買い物, 食べ物, 飲み物: name the verb, 物 makes it stuff.

lesson_examples.jp: 忘（わす）れ物（もの）　ない？
あの　建物（たてもの）は　何（なに）ですか？

勉.etymology: Phono-semantic: 免 (phonetic ベン; originally a birth — the ultimate strain) + 力 'strength' — straining with everything one has: exertion.
勉.mnemonic: Pushing with all your strength toward the escape hatch (免) — ベン. 勉強 is exactly that feeling, applied to a textbook.

lesson_examples.jp: いつから　フランス語（ご）　勉強（べんきょう）　し　てるの？
lesson_examples.en: When did you start studying French?

lesson_examples.jp: フランス語（ご）は　いつから　勉強（べんきょう）　し　てるの？
lesson_examples.en: When did you start studying French?

味.etymology: Phono-semantic: mouth (口) + 未 'not yet' (phonetic ミ) — what the mouth knows before words do: taste, flavor.
味.mnemonic: The tongue meets something it can't name yet (未): pure flavor — あじ. 意味 is the same tasting done by the mind: meaning.

lesson_examples.jp: どういう　意味（いみ）？
トムは　興味津々（きょうみしんしん）だ。

問.etymology: Phono-semantic: gate (門, phonetic モン) + mouth (口) — a mouth at the gate, calling in: to ask, to inquire.
問.mnemonic: Knock-knock at the gate: 'Anyone home?' — とう. Every 問題 starts as a mouth at a closed door.

lesson_examples.jp: 質問（しつもん）は　ありますか？
他（た）に　質問（しつもん）は　ありますか？
lesson_examples.en: Do you have any further questions?

薬.etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 楽 'comfort, ease' (phonetic ヤク) — the herb that restores ease: medicine.
薬.mnemonic: The plant (艹) that puts the music (楽) back in you — くすり. The 薬局 shelves are rows of bottled comfort.

lesson_examples.jp: この　近（ちか）くに　薬局（やっきょく）は　ありますか？
これは　薬局（やっきょく）です。

有.etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand (𠂇) holding meat (月) — having something in hand: to possess, to exist.
有.mnemonic: A fist closed around tonight's dinner: ownership at its most primal — ある, ユウ. 有名: possessed of a name everyone holds.

lesson_examples.jp: カリフォルニアは　果物（くだもの）で　有名（ゆうめい）です。
lesson_examples.en: California is famous for its fruit.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　有効（ゆうこう）です。

洋.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 羊 'sheep' (phonetic ヨウ) — waters vast as drifting flocks: the open ocean; and what came across it: the West.
洋.mnemonic: Whitecaps like a million sheep grazing to the horizon — ヨウ. Cross that flock and you reach 洋服, 洋食, 洋楽: the sheep-water world.

lesson_examples.jp: 洋服（ようふく）を　えらびます。
これは　洋品（ようひん）です。

旅.etymology: Compound ideograph: a banner with people marching beneath it — originally a military column of five hundred; the column on the move became the journey.
旅.mnemonic: Pack behind the flag and start walking — たび. 旅行 keeps the ancient column alive: everyone still follows the tour guide's little banner.

lesson_examples.jp: 旅行（りょこう）　どうでしたか？
旅行（りょこう）は　どうでしたか？

委.etymology: Compound ideograph: grain (禾) bending supple over a woman (女) — to bend to another's will: to entrust, delegate.
委.mnemonic: Hand your harvest over and let someone else carry it — イ. A 委員会 is a room of people holding everyone else's grain.

lesson_examples.jp: かかりを　委（まか）せます。
lesson_examples.en: I entrust the task to someone.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　委（ゆだ）ねる。

育.etymology: Compound ideograph: a child head-down at birth (𠫓) over flesh (月) — the newborn fed and grown: to raise, to be raised.
育.mnemonic: From the first upside-down cry, feeding flesh onto tiny bones — そだてる. 教育 raises the mind the same way.

lesson_examples.jp: 見（み）て、モーツァルトを　聴（き）いて　育（そだ）った　トマトだって。
lesson_examples.en: Look, a tomato which grew up listening to Mozart!

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　育（はぐく）む。

泳.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 永 'long, eternal' (phonetic エイ) — long strokes drawn through water: to swim.
泳.mnemonic: Stretch each stroke as long as forever (永) — およぐ. 水泳: eternity practiced in a 25-meter pool.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　泳（およ）いだ。
トムは　泳（およ）げない。

央.etymology: Pictograph: a person framed squarely inside a carrying-yoke — pinned at the exact middle: center.
央.mnemonic: Shoulders in the yoke, dead center by definition — オウ. 中央: the middle of the middle.

lesson_examples.jp: まちの　中央（ちゅうおう）に　ひろばが　ある。
lesson_examples.en: There's a square in the town center.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　中央（ちゅうおう）です。

横.etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 黄 (phonetic オウ) — the crossbar laid sideways across the gate: horizontal, side.
横.mnemonic: The yellow beam bolted crosswise on the frame — よこ. 横浜: the shore that runs sideways along the bay.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　通（とお）りを　横切（よこぎ）った。
まいにち　横（よこ）になる。

温.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 昷 (phonetic オン — read as a covered dish of warm food given kindly) — warmth, in water and in character.
温.mnemonic: A covered bowl of soup floated to someone who needs it — あたたかい. 温泉: the earth doing the same favor with a whole spring.

lesson_examples.jp: 気温（きおん）は　氷点下（ひょうてんか）　6度（ど）です。
気温（きおん）は　マイナス　6度（ど）です。

化.etymology: Compound ideograph: a person upright (亻) beside a person inverted (匕) — one being flipped into another state: transformation.
化.mnemonic: Same person, before and after the flip — ばける, カ. 文化 transforms people; 化学 transforms matter; 花 is 化 happening to a plant.

lesson_examples.jp: トムの　容体（ようだい）が　悪化（あっか）　した。
お化（ば）けって　信（しん）じますか？

荷.etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 何 (phonetic カ — itself originally 'to shoulder a load') — the bundle on the shoulder-pole: baggage; also the lotus.
荷.mnemonic: Stalks bound and slung on the pole 何 once pictured — に. 荷物: everything your shoulders answer for.

lesson_examples.jp: 切符（きっぷ）　買（か）ってくるから、ちょっと　荷物（にもつ）　見（み）てて。
lesson_examples.en: I'm going to go buy a ticket, so please watch my bags for a minute.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　荷造（にずく）りです。

meanings: counter for storeys of a building
階.etymology: Phono-semantic: mound (阝) + 皆 'all' (phonetic カイ) — steps cut up the slope, one for everyone: stairs; a building's floors.
階.mnemonic: Everybody (皆) climbing the terraced hill one step at a time — カイ. 二階, 三階: the hill moved indoors.

lesson_examples.jp: 男子（だんし）　トイレは　2階（かい）です。
lesson_examples.en: The men's room is on the second floor.

lesson_examples.jp: トムが　階段（かいだん）から　落（お）ちた。

感.etymology: Phono-semantic: 咸 'all, entire' (phonetic カン) + heart (心) — the heart moved entirely: feeling, sensation.
感.mnemonic: Not one corner of the heart left dry: total impact — カン. 感じる is when the whole 心 rings at once.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　責任感（せきにんかん）が　強（つよ）い。
lesson_examples.en: Tom has a strong sense of responsibility.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　感激（かんげき）　するだろう。

岸.etymology: Phono-semantic: mountain (山) and cliff (厂) + 干 (phonetic ガン) — where high ground breaks off at the water: the shore.
岸.mnemonic: Mountain, then cliff, then the drying line (干) where waves give up — きし. The land's last three strokes before the sea.

lesson_examples.jp: 川（かわ）の　岸（きし）を　あるきます。
これは　岸（きし）です。

期.etymology: Phono-semantic: 其 (phonetic キ) + moon (月) — time measured by the moon's fixed rounds: a set period, a term.
期.mnemonic: Mark the calendar by moons: this basket of days is one term — キ. 学期, 期間, 期待: hopes with a due date.

lesson_examples.jp: つぎの　学期（がっき）が　はじまります。
これは　同期（どうき）です。

客.etymology: Phono-semantic: roof (宀) + 各 'arrive' (phonetic キャク) — the one who arrives under your roof: guest, customer.
客.mnemonic: Footsteps arriving (各) under your roof: set another place — キャク. お客さん: the arrival you bow to.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　観客（かんきゃく）です。
これは　客観的（きゃっかんてき）だです。

球.etymology: Phono-semantic: jade (王) + 求 (phonetic キュウ) — jade ground into a perfect sphere: a ball, a globe.
球.mnemonic: Polish the gem until it rolls — たま, キュウ. 野球 sends it flying; 地球 is the one we stand on.

lesson_examples.jp: 野球（やきゅう）って　何（なに）が　面白（おもしろ）いの？
もしも　地球（ちきゅう）の　自転（じてん）が　止（と）まったら　どう　なると　思（おも）う？
lesson_examples.en: What do you think would happen if the earth stopped spinning?

級.etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 及 'reach up to' (phonetic キュウ) — threads graded length by length: rank, class.
級.mnemonic: Silk sorted by how far each strand reaches — キュウ. 上級, 初級: how far up the thread you've climbed.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　高級（こうきゅう）です。
これは　高級（こうきゅう）ブランドです。

橋.etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 喬 'tall, arching' (phonetic キョウ) — timber arched high over the water: a bridge.
橋.mnemonic: Wood bent into a high arc so boats pass under — はし. 日本橋: kilometer zero is a bridge.

lesson_examples.jp: 橋（はし）を　わたります。
これは　橋（はし）です。

局.etymology: Compound: a body bent (尸) into a cramped compartment — a partitioned room; hence the office, the bureau, and a 'board' situation (結局).
局.mnemonic: A clerk folded into a cubicle — キョク. 郵便局, 薬局: wherever there's a counter and a queue, there's a 局.

lesson_examples.jp: この　近（ちか）くに　薬局（やっきょく）は　ありますか？
郵便局（ゆうびんきょく）の　営業（えいぎょう）　時間（じかん）は　何時（なんじ）からですか？
lesson_examples.en: When does the post office open?

曲.etymology: Pictograph: a bent piece of basketwork or a carpenter's curved ruler — a bend; a melody is a line that bends.
曲.mnemonic: A basket seen edge-on, ribs curving — まがる. Music borrowed it: a 曲 is sound refusing to go straight.

lesson_examples.jp: 右（みぎ）に　曲（ま）がってください。
この　曲（きょく）　聞（き）いた　こと　ある？
lesson_examples.en: Have you listened to this song?

苦.etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 古 (phonetic ク) — the bitter old herb: bitterness; hence hardship, suffering.
苦.mnemonic: Chew the ancient weed and wince — にがい, くるしい. 苦労: life's aftertaste, prescribed daily.

lesson_examples.jp: 僕（ぼく）は　水泳（すいえい）が　苦手（にがて）です。
lesson_examples.en: I'm not very good at swimming.

lesson_examples.jp: 人前（ひとまえ）で　歌（うた）う　のは　苦手（にがて）です。
lesson_examples.en: I don't like to sing in public.

meanings: counter for armor, suits, sets of furniture
具.etymology: Compound ideograph: two hands offering up a vessel — implements presented ready for use: tool, equipment.
具.mnemonic: Both hands holding up the kit, ready to work — グ. 道具 for the craftsman, 家具 for the home, 具 in your soup: the stuff involved.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　具合（ぐあい）が　悪（わる）そうだ。
これは　家具（かぐ）です。

君.etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand holding the staff of office (尹) + mouth (口) — the one whose word commands: lord; softened into the familiar 'you' and the name-suffix 〜君.
君.mnemonic: Staff in hand, giving orders — きみ. Time demoted the lord into a schoolboy: 田中君, our young ruler of the classroom.

lesson_examples.jp: 君（きみ）なら　できるよ。
これは　君（きみ）です。

係.etymology: Compound: person (亻) + 系 'thread of connection' — the person tied by a thread to a duty: the one in charge.
係.mnemonic: A thread runs from the task to someone's wrist — かかり. Follow it and you find the 係の人, the person it's tied to.

lesson_examples.jp: トムには　関係（かんけい）　ない　んだ。
これは　関係（かんけい）です。

決.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 夬 'breach' (phonetic ケツ) — the dike cut and the water committed to one channel: to decide.
決.mnemonic: Break the dam: the water can never un-choose its path — きめる. 決して: 'never', said with the dike already cut.

lesson_examples.jp: 嘘（うそ）に　決（き）まっ　てんじゃん。
トムは　決（けっ）して　笑（わら）わない。

血.etymology: Compound ideograph: a drop falling into the ritual dish (皿) — sacrificial blood in the bowl: blood.
血.mnemonic: One dark drop over the bowl — ち. The dish under it makes it ceremony; the kanji never forgot the altar.

lesson_examples.jp: 鼻血（はなぢ）　出（で）　てるよ。
トムは　低（てい）　血圧（けつあつ）だ。

庫.etymology: Compound ideograph: carts (車) parked under a roof (广) — the arsenal and storehouse: warehouse.
庫.mnemonic: Wagons rolled in under one long roof — コ. 冷蔵庫: the household's coldest garage.

lesson_examples.jp: 冷蔵庫（れいぞうこ）の　中（なか）の　物（もの）は、何（なに）でも　御（ご）　自由（じゆう）に　召（め）し上（あ）がってください。
lesson_examples.en: Please feel free to have anything in the fridge.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　在庫（ざいこ）です。

湖.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 胡 (phonetic コ) — the great still water: a lake.
湖.mnemonic: Water so wide the far shore is a rumor — みずうみ. 琵琶湖: the lake shaped like a lute.

lesson_examples.jp: きれいな　湖（みずうみ）です。
これは　湖（みずうみ）です。

向.etymology: Pictograph: a house wall with its one window — the direction the window faces: to face, toward, yonder.
向.mnemonic: The house looks wherever its window does — むかう. 向こう is what the window sees: over there.

lesson_examples.jp: まどは　みなみに　向（む）いて　います。
これは　日向（ひなた）です。

幸.etymology: Pictograph of manacles — and the luck of escaping them: good fortune. Happiness, in the oldest script, is the shackle you were spared.
幸.mnemonic: The handcuffs that didn't close on you — しあわせ. 幸せ has always meant: it could have gone otherwise, and didn't.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　今（いま）　幸（しあわ）せ？
もっと　幸（しあわ）せに　なりたい。

港.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 巷 'lanes of a town' (phonetic コウ) — streets of water where ships park: a harbor.
港.mnemonic: The town's alleys continue straight into the sea, boats instead of carts — みなと. 空港: the same alleys, drawn in sky.

lesson_examples.jp: ふねが　港（みなと）に　います。
lesson_examples.en: A ship is at the harbor.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　港（みなと）です。

号.etymology: Simplified from 號: a mouth (口) with breath bending out (丂) — a cry, a call; hence a name called out, a numbered designation.
号.mnemonic: A shout with a hook on it: 'Number 5!' — ゴウ. Trains, typhoons and magazine issues all answer to their 号.

lesson_examples.jp: 信号（しんごう）　青（あお）に　なったよ。
電話（でんわ）　番号（ばんごう）を　教（おし）えてください。

根.etymology: Phono-semantic: tree (木) + 艮 'fixed, unyielding' (phonetic コン) — the part of the tree that refuses to move: the root.
根.mnemonic: Pull all you want: the stubborn (艮) part of the tree wins — ね. 大根: the vegetable that is entirely root and pride.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　屋根（やね）の　上（うえ）に　いる。
これは　根回（ねまわ）しです。

祭.etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand (又) laying meat (月) on the altar (示) — the offering rite: festival.
祭.mnemonic: The offering placed, the drums start — まつり. Every 祭 in Japan is this kanji with lanterns on.

lesson_examples.jp: なつ祭（まつ）りに　いきます。
lesson_examples.en: I go to the summer festival.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　祭（まつ）りです。

坂.etymology: Phono-semantic: earth (土) + 反 (phonetic ハン) — ground tilted against you: a slope.
坂.mnemonic: The ground pushes back (反) at every step: uphill — さか. 大阪: the big slope that became a big city.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　坂（さか）です。
坂（さか）が　すきです。

皿.etymology: Pictograph: a shallow dish on its stand, seen from the side — plate, and counter for helpings.
皿.mnemonic: A serving plate drawn in cross-section, food-side up — さら. At the sushi bar you are billed by the stack of 皿.

lesson_examples.jp: お　皿（さら）が　汚（よご）れています。
これは　皿（さら）です。

指.etymology: Phono-semantic: hand (扌) + 旨 (phonetic シ) — the hand's pointers: fingers; to point, to indicate.
指.mnemonic: The part of the hand that knows what it wants (旨) — ゆび. 指す points, 指輪 rings it, 指定 pins the seat.

lesson_examples.jp: ご　指摘（してき）　ありがとうございます。
これは　指図（さしず）です。

歯.etymology: Phono-semantic (simplified from 齒): 止 (phonetic シ) over a pictograph of teeth in an open mouth — tooth.
歯.mnemonic: Open wide: rice grains of enamel in their box — は. The 歯医者 is the only person paid to look in there.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　歯（は）が　痛（いた）い。
トムは　歯（は）を　磨（みが）いている。

次.etymology: Compound: two (二→冫) + a person pausing open-mouthed (欠) — the second stop, the one after: next.
次.mnemonic: Catch your breath, then the second leg — つぎ. 次の駅: the station your yawn arrives at.

lesson_examples.jp: 次（つぎ）の　交差点（こうさてん）を　右（みぎ）に　曲（ま）がってください。
lesson_examples.en: Turn right at the next intersection.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　次（つ）ぐ。

式.etymology: Phono-semantic: 弋 'marker stake' + 工 'work' (phonetic シキ) — work done to the staked-out pattern: the set form, a ceremony, a formula.
式.mnemonic: Stakes out, string taut, everyone follows the pattern — シキ. Weddings (結婚式) and equations (数式) run on the same rails.

lesson_examples.jp: 結婚式（けっこんしき）は　土曜日（どようび）に　行（おこな）われます。
lesson_examples.en: The wedding will take place on Saturday.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　格式（かくしき）です。

実.etymology: Simplified from 實: a house (宀) strung full of coins (貫) — a filled house: substance; the plant's substance is its fruit; the fact's substance is reality.
実.mnemonic: The house is actually full — み, the fruit; ジツ, the fact. 実は…: 'here's what's really in the house.'

lesson_examples.jp: 悲（かな）しい　ことですが、真実（しんじつ）です。
この　物語（ものがたり）は　実話（じつわ）に　基（もと）づいています。
lesson_examples.en: This story is based on a true story.

取.etymology: Compound ideograph: an ear (耳) in a hand (又) — warriors took the ears of the fallen as proof: to take, grimly literal.
取.mnemonic: A hand closes on an ear and doesn't let go — とる. Modern life softened it to 取る a photo, 受け取る a parcel.

lesson_examples.jp: それ　取（と）ってくれる？
はさみを　取（と）って下（くだ）さい。

守.etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand (寸) under the roof (宀) — the hand that keeps the house: to guard, to keep (a promise).
守.mnemonic: One hand on the door, all night — まもる. お守り: the shrine sells you that hand, folded in brocade.

lesson_examples.jp: やくそくを　守（まも）ります。
まいにち　守（まも）る。

酒.etymology: Compound: liquid (氵) + the wine jar (酉, a pictograph of the fermenting vessel) — the jar's liquid: alcohol.
酒.mnemonic: What the ancient jar (酉) sweats out — さけ. 居酒屋: the room built around that jar.

lesson_examples.jp: お　酒（さけ）は　飲（の）まれますか？
これは　酒（さけ）です。

受.etymology: Compound ideograph: one hand (爫) passing a tray (冖) to another hand (又) — the handover: to receive, accept.
受.mnemonic: Two hands, one tray, mid-air — うける. 受験 is holding your tray out to an exam board.

lesson_examples.jp: トムの　言（い）う　ことなんか　真（しん）に　受（う）けちゃ　だめだよ。
lesson_examples.en: You shouldn't take the things Tom says seriously.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　受（う）ける。

州.etymology: Pictograph: the river (川) with sandbar islets (the dots) — settled sandbanks became districts: province, state.
州.mnemonic: Three islands anchored in the current — シュウ. 九州: nine of them, grown into a region; アメリカの州: fifty.

lesson_examples.jp: かわの　中州（なかす）に　とりが　いる。
lesson_examples.en: There are birds on the sandbar.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　州（す）です。

拾.etymology: Phono-semantic: hand (扌) + 合 'fit' (phonetic シュウ) — the hand closing on what it finds: to pick up. Also the formal legal 'ten'.
拾.mnemonic: Hand meets object, perfect fit: yours now — ひろう. On contracts it moonlights as an unforgeable 十.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　拾（ひろ）う。
わたしは　よく　拾（ひろ）う。

宿.etymology: Compound ideograph: a person (亻) on a mat (百-shaped bedding) under a roof (宀) — a traveler bedded down: lodging, an inn.
宿.mnemonic: One roof, one stranger, one rented futon — やど. 新宿: the 'new inn' that became three million beds; 宿題 the homework you lodge overnight.

lesson_examples.jp: すみません、宿題（しゅくだい）　忘（わす）れました。
lesson_examples.en: I'm sorry, I forgot to do my homework.

lesson_examples.jp: 明日（あした）の　英語（えいご）って　宿題（しゅくだい）　あったっけ？
lesson_examples.en: Did we have any English homework that needs to be done by tomorrow?

助.etymology: Phono-semantic: 且 (phonetic ジョ) + strength (力) — strength added from the side: to help.
助.mnemonic: Your load, plus someone else's muscle sliding under it — たすける. 助けて! calls for exactly one more 力.

lesson_examples.jp: 助（たす）けてください。
そうして　いただけると　助（たす）かります。
lesson_examples.en: It would be much appreciated if you would do that for me.

勝.etymology: Phono-semantic: a phonetic (朕) + strength (力) — strength that lifts and prevails: to win.
勝.mnemonic: Muscle under the load until it rises: victory — かつ. 勝負 pairs this kanji with its shadow, defeat.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　勝（か）った。
トムは　勝（か）った？

商.etymology: Originally the emblem of the Shang (商) people — after their kingdom fell, they wandered as traders, and their name became the word for commerce.
商.mnemonic: A whole fallen dynasty setting up market stalls — ショウ. 商売: history's plan B, still in business.

lesson_examples.jp: 商売（しょうばい）は　じゅんちょうです。
これは　商品（しょうひん）です。

消.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 肖 'shrink, resemble-less' (phonetic ショウ) — doused down to nothing: to extinguish, erase, vanish.
消.mnemonic: Water on the flame until nothing is left to resemble it — けす. 消しゴム erases pencil; 消える erases anything.

lesson_examples.jp: 電気（でんき）　消（け）しても　いい？
lesson_examples.en: Do you mind if I turn off the light?

lesson_examples.jp: テレビ　消（け）しても　いい？
lesson_examples.en: Can I turn off the TV?

章.etymology: Originally a tattooing needle making its mark — a distinguishing sign: a badge; in texts, the marked-off unit: a chapter.
章.mnemonic: The stamp pressed at the end of a section: this part is sealed — ショウ. Chapters and medals are the same thing: marks that say 'unit complete'.

lesson_examples.jp: この　文章（ぶんしょう）を　訳（やく）してもらえませんか？
lesson_examples.en: Could you translate this sentence for me?

lesson_examples.jp: これは　文章（ぶんしょう）です。
lesson_examples.en: This is a piece of writing.

植.etymology: Phono-semantic: tree (木) + 直 'straight' (phonetic ショク) — setting a sapling in straight: to plant.
植.mnemonic: Hold the sapling plumb-straight (直) while the soil goes in — うえる. 植物: everything that got planted and stayed.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　植（う）える。
これは　植物（しょくぶつ）です。

深.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 罙 'reach far in' (phonetic シン) — water you can reach into without touching bottom: deep.
深.mnemonic: Arm in to the shoulder and still no floor — ふかい. Deep water, deep night (深夜), deep thoughts: same missing bottom.

lesson_examples.jp: その　池（いけ）は　深（ふか）さ　3　mです。
これは　深刻（しんこく）です。

申.etymology: Pictograph: forked lightning stretching down — the gods declaring themselves; hence to state (humbly, 申す), and the zodiac monkey by borrowing.
申.mnemonic: Lightning speaks first, you answer politely — もうす. 申します: introducing yourself under a sky that outranks you.

lesson_examples.jp: 遅（おく）れて　申（もう）し訳（わけ）　ありません。
lesson_examples.en: Please pardon me for coming late.

lesson_examples.jp: 遅刻（ちこく）　して　申（もう）し訳（わけ）　ありません。
lesson_examples.en: Please excuse me for coming late.

神.etymology: Phono-semantic: altar (示/ネ) + 申 'lightning' (phonetic シン) — the power addressed at the altar, announced in lightning: the gods.
神.mnemonic: Where lightning meets the altar — かみ. 神社 is the address; 神様 the resident.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　神話（しんわ）です。
これは　精神的（せいしんてき）です。

身.etymology: Pictograph: a torso in profile with a full belly — originally a pregnant body: the living body, one's person.
身.mnemonic: A silhouette carrying life in its belly — み. 身体 is the body; 中身 the body of anything — what's carried inside.

lesson_examples.jp: 独身（どくしん）ですか。
身長（しんちょう）　何（なん）センチ？

整.etymology: Compound: a bundle (束) tapped by a hand (攵) until correct (正) — knocked into order: to arrange, adjust.
整.mnemonic: Tap the stack square on the desk until every edge is 正 — ととのえる. 整理: the satisfying thunk of order.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　整（ととの）える。
これは　整備（せいび）です。

昔.etymology: Compound ideograph: layers (廿) piled over days (日) — days heaped on days: long ago, antiquity.
昔.mnemonic: Day pressed on day like sediment — むかし. Every folktale drills into the same stratum: 昔々, once upon a time.

lesson_examples.jp: 昔（むかし）の　はなしを　ききます。
lesson_examples.en: I listen to tales of long ago.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　昔（むかし）です。
lesson_examples.en: This is once upon a time.

全.etymology: Compound ideograph: flawless jade (王) kept under cover (𠆢) — intact, untouched: whole, complete.
全.mnemonic: The gem still in its case, not a scratch — ゼン. 全部, 全然, 安全: wholeness, in stock, on sale, and kept safe.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　全（すべ）てを　否定（ひてい）　した。
トムは　全速力（ぜんそくりょく）で　走（はし）った。

想.etymology: Phono-semantic: 相 'facing, mutual' (phonetic ソウ) + heart (心) — the heart facing an image of what isn't there: to imagine, conceive.
想.mnemonic: The heart holds a picture up and studies it — ソウ. 思想 is a gallery of them; 可哀想 is the picture that hurts to look at.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　感想（かんそう）です。
これは　発想（はっそう）です。

相.etymology: Compound ideograph: an eye (目) examining a tree (木) — observer and observed facing each other: mutual, reciprocal; an aspect; a minister who 'oversees'.
相.mnemonic: You look at the tree; on some level the tree looks back — あい. 相手: the one on the other end of your gaze.

lesson_examples.jp: 相変（あいか）わらず　忙（いそが）しいの？
これは　相子（あいこ）です。

息.etymology: Compound ideograph: nose (自) over heart (心) — the current running between nose and heart: breath; a son (one's own breath continued).
息.mnemonic: Air rides from the nose down to the heart and back — いき. 休息 is when you finally hear it; 息子 is your breath walking around outside you.

lesson_examples.jp: 息（いき）を　止（と）めてください。
トムは　ため息（いき）を　ついた。

速.etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 束 'tied bundle' (phonetic ソク) — strapped tight and speeding: fast.
速.mnemonic: Cinch the pack down and nothing rattles: pure speed — はやい. The 高速 is where tight bundles overtake loose ones.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　足（あし）が　速（はや）い。
トムは　頭（あたま）の　回転（かいてん）が　速（はや）い。
lesson_examples.en: Tom has a good head on his shoulders.

他.etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 也 (phonetic タ) — some person over there, not this one: other.
他.mnemonic: A figure trailing off in another direction — ほか. その他: everyone and everything the sentence didn't name.

lesson_examples.jp: 他（た）に　質問（しつもん）は　ありますか？
lesson_examples.en: Do you have any further questions?

lesson_examples.jp: 他（た）に　何（なに）か　聞（き）きたい　こと　ある？
lesson_examples.en: Do you have any other questions?

打.etymology: Phono-semantic: hand (扌) + 丁 'nail' (phonetic ダ/チョウ) — the hand coming down on the nail: to strike.
打.mnemonic: Hammer-hand meets nail head — うつ. Baseball took it (打つ, batting), and so did your keyboard: 打ち込む.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　三塁打（さんるいだ）を　打（う）った。
まいにち　打（う）つ。

対.etymology: Simplified from 對: a hand (寸) answering a rack of bells — to respond in kind, face to face: versus, vis-à-vis.
対.mnemonic: Two players squared up across the table — タイ. 3対2, 反対, 対する: everything that stands facing something else.

lesson_examples.jp: トムには　絶対（ぜったい）　内緒（ないしょ）だよ。
lesson_examples.en: No matter what, don't tell Tom.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　対等（たいとう）です。

第.etymology: Phono-semantic: bamboo (⺮) + 弟 'birth-order' (phonetic ダイ) — bamboo slips filed in sequence: number so-and-so.
第.mnemonic: The bamboo tags on a string, each with its rank — ダイ. 第一 hangs first; everything else queues behind it.

lesson_examples.jp: 第（だい）1回（かい）の　たいかいです。
これは　第一（だいいち）です。

炭.etymology: Compound: fire (火) burning under the mountain's cliff (山+厂) — the kiln in the hillside: charcoal, coal.
炭.mnemonic: Fire sealed in the hill until wood turns black and light — すみ. The yakitori grill still runs on this kanji.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　炭（すみ）です。
炭（すみ）が　すきです。

談.etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 炎 'blaze' (phonetic ダン) — talk by the fire, or talk that catches like one: discussion.
談.mnemonic: Words traded across a campfire, sparks included — ダン. 相談 is bringing your problem to that fire.

lesson_examples.jp: ごめん、軽（かる）い　冗談（じょうだん）の　つもりだった　んだけど。
lesson_examples.en: Sorry, I only meant it as a joke.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　縁談（えんだん）です。

柱.etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 主 'master' (phonetic チュウ) — the master timber the whole house hangs on: the pillar.
柱.mnemonic: One post holds the roof the way the master holds the household — はしら. Remove it and everything above remembers why it mattered.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　柱（はしら）です。
柱（はしら）が　すきです。

調.etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 周 'all the way around' (phonetic チョウ) — checking a thing from every side: to tune, adjust, investigate.
調.mnemonic: Walk your questions all the way around it (周) until it sounds right — しらべる. 調べる investigates; 調子 is the tuning you're in today.

lesson_examples.jp: 人（ひと）に　聞（き）く　前（まえ）に　少（すこ）しは　自分（じぶん）で　調（しら）べたら？
lesson_examples.en: How about doing a bit of research on your own before asking for help?

lesson_examples.jp: この　ピアノ　何年（なんねん）　調律（ちょうりつ）　し　てない　んだろうね。
lesson_examples.en: This piano has probably not been tuned for years.

追.etymology: Compound: movement (辶) + 𠂤 'massed troops' — marching after a retreating column: to pursue, chase.
追.mnemonic: Their dust cloud is still visible — go! — おう. 追いかける: the whole kanji at a sprint.

lesson_examples.jp: ゆめを　追（お）います。
これは　追放（ついほう）です。

定.etymology: Compound ideograph: things set correct (正) under the roof (宀) — settled in place: fixed, determined.
定.mnemonic: Everything in the house squared and bolted — さだめる, テイ. 予定, 定食: the schedule and the set meal — life pre-decided.

lesson_examples.jp: 本日（ほんじつ）は　定休日（ていきゅうび）です。
今日（きょう）の　夜（よる）　予定（よてい）　ある？
lesson_examples.en: Do you have plans for tonight?

庭.etymology: Phono-semantic: building (广) + 廷 'royal court' (phonetic テイ) — the open ground within the walls: courtyard, garden.
庭.mnemonic: The palace court shrunk to fit behind your house — にわ. Every 庭 keeps a little ceremony in its gravel.

lesson_examples.jp: 庭（にわ）に　はなを　うえます。
lesson_examples.en: I plant flowers in the garden.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　庭（にわ）です。

鉄.etymology: Simplified from 鐵: metal (金) + a phonetic now written 失 — the workhorse metal: iron.
鉄.mnemonic: The metal that loses (失) its shine and keeps its strength — てつ. 地下鉄: iron veins under the city.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　私鉄（してつ）です。
これは　地下鉄（ちかてつ）です。

登.etymology: Compound ideograph: feet set apart (癶) climbing with the offering vessel (豆) — mounting the altar steps: to ascend.
登.mnemonic: Step by step up the shrine stairs, bowl held level — のぼる. 登山 is the same climb with a bigger altar.

lesson_examples.jp: 明日（あした）は　山登（やまのぼ）りに　行（い）ってきます。
lesson_examples.en: I'm going to go mountain climbing tomorrow.

lesson_examples.jp: 富士山（ふじさん）に　登（のぼ）った　ことは　ありますか？
lesson_examples.en: Have you ever climbed Mt. Fuji?

島.etymology: Compound ideograph: a bird (鳥, tail clipped) on a mountain (山) rising from the sea — where seabirds rest: an island.
島.mnemonic: A peak just big enough for the gulls to land — しま. Japan: one country, 14,000 of these kanji.

lesson_examples.jp: 島（しま）に　わたります。
これは　島（しま）です。

投.etymology: Compound ideograph: hand (扌) + 殳 'lance' — the hand hurling the weapon: to throw.
投.mnemonic: Wind-up, release: spear away — なげる. The pitcher (投手) does it for a living, mercifully with a ball.

lesson_examples.jp: トムには　投票権（とうひょうけん）が　ある。
lesson_examples.en: Tom has the right to vote.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　投稿（とうこう）です。

湯.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 昜 'sun blazing up' (phonetic トウ) — water with the sun in it: hot water.
湯.mnemonic: Water heated until it glows like sunrise — ゆ. The ♨ sign and the sentō curtain both spell this one kanji.

lesson_examples.jp: 湯（ゆ）が　あついです。
これは　湯（ゆ）です。

等.etymology: Compound: bamboo slips (⺮) sorted at the office (寺) — graded into equal ranks: equal; 'and the rest of the same grade': etc.
等.mnemonic: Slips of the same length in the same box — ひとしい. 一等 is the top box; 等々 waves at all the boxes you didn't list.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　等（ひと）しいです。
これは　対等（たいとう）です。

童.etymology: Grim origin: a tattooed (辛-marked) servant child; the meaning softened over centuries to simply 'child'.
童.mnemonic: The kanji grew up gentler than it was born: now it just means kids — わらべ, ドウ. 児童 in school, 童話 at bedtime.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　児童（じどう）です。
これは　童（わらべ）です。

農.etymology: Compound ideograph: field rows worked with the shell-hoe (辰 — a clamshell blade) — dawn labor on the land: agriculture.
農.mnemonic: A clamshell lashed to a stick, scraping rows before sunrise — ノウ. 農家: the people who fed everyone with a seashell.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　農家（のうか）です。
これは　農業（のうぎょう）です。

波.etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 皮 'skin' (phonetic ハ) — the sea's moving skin: waves.
波.mnemonic: The ocean flexing its hide — なみ. Radio waves, heat waves, 津波: everything that travels as rolling skin.

lesson_examples.jp: 波（なみ）の　おとが　きこえます。
lesson_examples.en: I can hear the sound of the waves.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　波（なみ）です。

配.etymology: Compound ideograph: an attendant (己) kneeling at the wine jar (酉), portioning it out — to distribute, allot; the allotted partner: spouse.
配.mnemonic: Cup by cup around the table, no one skipped — くばる. 心配 is your heart doing rounds it wasn't asked to do.

lesson_examples.jp: 心配（しんぱい）　しないで。
何（なに）が　心配（しんぱい）なの？

倍.etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 咅 (phonetic バイ) — originally to split away, and a thing split makes two: double, -fold.
倍.mnemonic: Cut the mochi in half: now you have two — バイ. 二倍, 三倍: multiplication by cheerful cutting.

lesson_examples.jp: 2倍（ばい）です。
これは　倍（ばい）です。

箱.etymology: Phono-semantic: bamboo (⺮) + 相 (phonetic ソウ→はこ) — the woven bamboo chest: a box.
箱.mnemonic: Bamboo strips facing each other (相) until they close into walls — はこ. 箱根: the box canyon with hot springs in it.

lesson_examples.jp: 一箱（いちはこ）　いくらですか？
lesson_examples.en: How much is it per box?

lesson_examples.jp: この　箱（はこ）には　何（なに）が　入（はい）っ　てるの？

畑.etymology: A kokuji — invented in Japan: fire (火) + field (田) — land cleared by burning for dry crops (no paddy water): a farm field.
畑.mnemonic: Burn the brush, plant the slope: the dry field — はたけ. Japan built this kanji itself, ash and all.

lesson_examples.jp: 畑（はたけ）で　やさいを　そだてます。
lesson_examples.en: We grow vegetables in the field.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　畑（はた）です。

反.etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand (又) pressed against the cliff (厂), pushing back — to turn over, oppose: anti-.
反.mnemonic: Palm flat on the rock face, shoving the other way — ハン. 反対 is the shove made official.

lesson_examples.jp: はんたいの　いけんに　反論（はんろん）します。
lesson_examples.en: I argue against the opposing view.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　反（そ）らす。

板.etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 反 (phonetic ハン) — wood flipped and planed flat: a board.
板.mnemonic: Turn the log, shave; turn, shave — until it's a plank — いた. The 黒板 and the 掲示板 are its indoor careers.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　板（いた）です。
これは　俎板（まないた）です。

悲.etymology: Phono-semantic: 非 'pulled apart in two directions' (phonetic ヒ) + heart (心) — a heart split open: sorrow.
悲.mnemonic: Two wings tearing away from each other with the heart between — かなしい. Grief is the heart's wishbone moment.

lesson_examples.jp: 何（なに）が　そんなに　悲（かな）しいの？
悲（かな）しい　お知（し）らせが　あります。

皮.etymology: Pictograph: a hand stripping the hide from a carcass — skin, pelt, bark, peel.
皮.mnemonic: The hand at the bottom is mid-peel — かわ. Banana skin, tree bark, dumpling wrapper: all 皮 to Japanese.

lesson_examples.jp: りんごの　皮（かわ）を　むきます。
これは　皮（かわ）です。

美.etymology: Compound ideograph: a big (大) sheep (羊) — the fattest, finest animal brought for offering: fine, beautiful.
美.mnemonic: The prize sheep, groomed and gleaming, led up the aisle — うつくしい. Beauty began as the best thing you could give.

lesson_examples.jp: この　美術館（びじゅつかん）の　入場料（にゅうじょうりょう）は　30ドルです。
lesson_examples.en: Admission to the museum is thirty dollars.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　美味（うま）いです。

鼻.etymology: Phono-semantic: 自 (the original nose pictograph) + 畀 (phonetic ビ) — added when 自 drifted off to mean 'oneself': the nose proper.
鼻.mnemonic: The old nose (自) needed scaffolding once 'self' stole it: behold the full apparatus — はな. Biggest kanji on the face.

lesson_examples.jp: 鼻血（はなぢ）　出（で）　てるよ。
まいにち　鼻（はな）にかける。

筆.etymology: Compound ideograph: bamboo (⺮) + 聿 'hand gripping a brush' — the bamboo-handled writing brush.
筆.mnemonic: Bamboo shaft, wolf-hair tip, hand steady — ふで. The 鉛筆 is its graphite grandchild.

lesson_examples.jp: 鉛筆（えんぴつ）で　書（か）いて下（くだ）さい。
みんな　鉛筆（えんぴつ）　持（も）っ　てる？

氷.etymology: Compound: water (水) with a single freezing drop added — water gone solid: ice.
氷.mnemonic: Water with one extra chip in it: frozen — こおり. The shaved-ice flags of summer fly this kanji, かき氷.

lesson_examples.jp: 気温（きおん）は　氷点下（ひょうてんか）　6度（ど）です。
これは　氷（こおり）です。

表.etymology: Compound ideograph: a garment (衣) worn fur-side out — the outside face of things: surface, exterior; what is displayed: a chart, a table.
表.mnemonic: Wear the coat fur-out and everyone sees your outside — おもて, ヒョウ. 発表 is turning your inside out on purpose.

lesson_examples.jp: きもちを　ことばで　表（あらわ）します。
lesson_examples.en: I express my feelings in words.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　表札（ひょうさつ）です。

秒.etymology: Compound: grain (禾) + 少 'tiny' — originally the hair-thin awn at the grain's tip; adopted for the thinnest slice of time: the second.
秒.mnemonic: Time shaved as fine as the whisker on a rice grain — ビョウ. 一秒: one awn's worth of your life.

lesson_examples.jp: 1分（ふん）は　60秒（びょう）です。
トム、10秒（びょう）で　いいから　黙（だま）っ　ててくれない？
lesson_examples.en: Tom, could you shut up for just ten seconds?

負.etymology: Compound ideograph: a person bent over a cowrie (貝) — shouldering a debt: to bear a burden; the one who carries the loss: defeat.
負.mnemonic: Bowed under the moneylender's shell — まける. To lose is to carry; 勝負 asks who walks away upright.

lesson_examples.jp: トムが　負（ま）けた。
まいにち　負（お）う。

meanings: counter for copies of a newspaper or magazine
部.etymology: Phono-semantic: 咅 (phonetic ブ) + city (阝) — one district of the town: a section, department; in school, the club.
部.mnemonic: The town carved into wards, your name on one — ブ. 全部 is all the wards at once; 部活 the ward you sweat for after class.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　部屋（へや）を　見回（みまわ）した。
値段（ねだん）は　全部（ぜんぶ）　同（おな）じな　んですか？
lesson_examples.en: Are they all the same price?

福.etymology: Phono-semantic: altar (示/ネ) + 畐 'jar filled to the brim' (phonetic フク) — abundance granted at the altar: blessing, good fortune.
福.mnemonic: The offering jar comes back from the altar full — フク. 福 is what spills over; 幸福 when it spills on you.

lesson_examples.jp: 「福（ふく）は　うち。」と　いいます。
これは　福祉（ふくし）です。

平.etymology: Pictograph read as a balance at rest — or duckweed lying flat on water: level, even, calm.
平.mnemonic: The scale's beam dead level, nothing trembling — たいら, ヘイ. 平和 is that stillness scaled up to nations.

lesson_examples.jp: そんな　の　不公平（ふこうへい）じゃない？
これは　公平（こうへい）です。

返.etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 反 'flip' (phonetic ヘン) — walking the road flipped around: to return something, to reply.
返.mnemonic: Same road, reversed footage — かえす. 返事 is words making the return trip.

lesson_examples.jp: トムから　返事（へんじ）　来（き）た？
セーターが　裏返（うらがえ）しだよ。
lesson_examples.en: You're wearing your sweater inside out.

放.etymology: Phono-semantic: 方 'direction' (phonetic ホウ) + 攵 'hand with stick' — driven off toward the horizon: to release, let go, banish.
放.mnemonic: A tap of the stick and it bolts for open country — はなす. 放送 releases voices into the air on purpose.

lesson_examples.jp: 絶賛（ぜっさん）　放送中（ほうそうちゅう）！
まいにち　放（はな）す。

命.etymology: Compound ideograph: an order (口) spoken from above the assembly (亼) to one kneeling (卩) — the command; and the allotted span it decrees: life, fate.
命.mnemonic: The decree read out while you kneel: this much time, this path — いのち. Life, in the old script, is an order you receive.

lesson_examples.jp: 命（いのち）を　まもります。
これは　運命（うんめい）です。

面.etymology: Pictograph: a face framed by its outline with one eye showing — the face; a mask; any facing surface or aspect.
面.mnemonic: An eye peering from inside the frame of a Noh mask — メン. 場面, 画面, 真面目: scenes, screens and the earnest face you keep on.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　面食（めんく）いだ。
lesson_examples.en: Tom is only interested in good-looking girls.

lesson_examples.jp: 野球（やきゅう）って　何（なに）が　面白（おもしろ）いの？

役.etymology: Compound ideograph: marching (彳) with a weapon (殳) — pressed into service: duty, office; the part one is assigned: a role.
役.mnemonic: Shouldering the spear because your number came up — ヤク. On stage the draft is kinder: 役 is just your role.

lesson_examples.jp: お　役（やく）に　立（た）てて　うれしいです。
lesson_examples.en: I'm glad I could be of service.

lesson_examples.jp: お　役（やく）に　立（た）ててよかったです。

油.etymology: Phono-semantic: liquid (氵) + 由 (phonetic ユ) — the slick liquid: oil.
油.mnemonic: A liquid with its own agenda (由): it floats, it clings, it burns — あぶら. 醤油: the oil-like sauce that runs Japan.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　油断（ゆだん）です。
これは　醤油（しょうゆ）です。

由.etymology: Origin debated — a gourd putting out its sprout, or a wick rising from a lamp; since antiquity it has meant the 'whence': cause, reason, via.
由.mnemonic: The sprout shows where the vine came from — ユ. 理由 is the sprout of any claim; 自由 is growing wherever you please.

lesson_examples.jp: 理由（りゆう）　聞（き）いても　いい？
ご　自由（じゆう）に　おとり　ください。
lesson_examples.en: You can have it for nothing.

遊.etymology: Phono-semantic: movement (辶) + 斿 'banner streaming, child beneath' (phonetic ユウ) — drifting like a flag on the wind: to roam, to play.
遊.mnemonic: A kid trailing a streamer, going nowhere in particular, perfectly — あそぶ. 遊園地: the industrial complex of exactly that.

lesson_examples.jp: マッチで　遊（あそ）んでは　いけません。
来週（らいしゅう）の　日曜日（にちようび）に　遊（あそ）びに　来（き）てください。
lesson_examples.en: Come and see me on Sunday next week.

予.etymology: Pictograph read as a weaver's shuttle handed forward — what is passed ahead of the weave: beforehand, in advance.
予.mnemonic: The shuttle is already through before the thread arrives — ヨ. 予定, 予約, 天気予報: tomorrow, pre-threaded.

lesson_examples.jp: 今日（きょう）の　夜（よる）　予定（よてい）　ある？
lesson_examples.en: Do you have plans for tonight?

lesson_examples.jp: 明日（あした）は　何（なに）か　予定（よてい）　ある？
lesson_examples.en: Do you have any plans for tomorrow?

様.etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + a phonetic (羕, ヨウ) — the pattern of the grain: manner, appearance; extended into the honorific 〜様.
様.mnemonic: Every tree's grain flows its own way: its manner — ヨウ. Address people by their grain: 田中様, treated wood-grain-up.

lesson_examples.jp: お疲（つか）れ様（さま）。
お母様（かあさま）の　旧姓（きゅうせい）は　何（なに）ですか？

葉.etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 枼 'thin slats on a tree' (phonetic ヨウ) — the tree's thin green plates: leaves.
葉.mnemonic: Generations (世) budding off the tree in flat green sheets — は. 言葉: words are the leaves the mouth puts out.

lesson_examples.jp: その　言葉（ことば）は　初耳（はつみみ）です。
lesson_examples.en: This is the first time I've heard that word.

lesson_examples.jp: その　言葉（ことば）は　初（はじ）めて　聞（き）きました。
lesson_examples.en: This is the first time I've heard that word.

陽.etymology: Phono-semantic: mound (阝) + 昜 'sun blazing up' (phonetic ヨウ) — the sunlit south face of the hill: sunshine, the yang principle.
陽.mnemonic: The bright side of the slope, where snow gives up first — ヨウ. 太陽: the source of every south face.

lesson_examples.jp: こんな　きれいな　夕陽（ゆうひ）　見（み）た　こと　ないよ。
lesson_examples.en: I've never seen such a beautiful sunset.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　陽気（ようき）です。

落.etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 洛 (phonetic ラク) — leaves letting go one by one: to fall, drop, fail.
落.mnemonic: Every leaf reaches the same conclusion separately — おちる. 落ち着く is falling until you settle, calm at last.

lesson_examples.jp: トムは　落（お）っこちた。
トムが　落（お）っこちた。

流.etymology: Compound: water (氵) + 㐬 — a newborn head-down with hair streaming — carried off by the water: current, to flow.
流.mnemonic: Hair streaming in the current, everything swept one way — ながれる. Styles, rumors and rivers all 流れる.

lesson_examples.jp: かわが　流（なが）れます。
これは　流（なが）しです。

meanings: counter for carriages (e.g., in a train)
両.etymology: Simplified from 兩: a yoke or scale-beam holding two sides in balance — both; an old coin weighed on such scales.
両.mnemonic: One beam, two pans, matched — リョウ. 両手, 両親, 両方: hands, parents, sides — the things that come in balanced pairs.

lesson_examples.jp: 両手（りょうて）で　もちます。
lesson_examples.en: I hold it with both hands.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　両立（りょうりつ）です。

緑.etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 彔 (phonetic リョク) — silk dyed the color of young growth: green.
緑.mnemonic: Thread pulled from the dye-vat dripping spring color — みどり. The Yamanote line runs on rails of this kanji.

lesson_examples.jp: 緑（みどり）の　森（もり）が　ひろがる。
これは　緑（みどり）です。

礼.etymology: Simplified from 禮: altar (示) + ritual vessel (豊) — the proper conduct of the rite: etiquette, the bow, thanks.
礼.mnemonic: At the altar, the body folds on the little hook: the bow — レイ. お礼 is that hook offered to a person instead of a god.

lesson_examples.jp: お礼（れい）を　いいます。
これは　無礼（ぶれい）です。

列.etymology: Compound ideograph: bones (歹) laid out in order by the blade (刂) — things arranged in sequence: a row, a file.
列.mnemonic: The surgeon's tray: everything in its grim, tidy line — レツ. 行列 is the human version: the queue.

lesson_examples.jp: すみません、これ　何（なに）の　列（れつ）ですか？
lesson_examples.en: Excuse me, what queue is this?

lesson_examples.jp: これは　列（れつ）です。

練.etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 柬 (phonetic レン) — raw silk boiled and worked until supple: to refine; refining yourself: practice.
練.mnemonic: Boil the silk, work it, boil it again: softness is earned — レン. 練習 does to you what the vat does to thread.

lesson_examples.jp: まいにち　練（ね）る。
これは　未練（みれん）です。

路.etymology: Phono-semantic: foot (足) + 各 'arrive' (phonetic ロ) — where feet arrive one after another: the road, the route.
路.mnemonic: Feet arriving in each other's prints until the ground remembers — ロ. 道路 doubles it; 線路 lays it in steel.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　路線（ろせん）です。
これは　通路（つうろ）です。

和.etymology: Phono-semantic: grain (禾, phonetic ワ) + mouth (口) — grain shared among mouths: peace, harmony; the name Japan chose for its own style: 和.
和.mnemonic: Rice enough for every mouth at the table — ワ. 平和 is the treaty; 和食, 和室, 和風: harmony you can eat, sit in, and decorate with.

lesson_examples.jp: 和風（わふう）の　にわですね。
まいにち　和（やわ）らげる。

宮.etymology: Compound ideograph: many rooms (呂) under one great roof (宀) — a palace; the god's palace: a shrine.
宮.mnemonic: Room after room under the sacred roof — みや. 宮崎, 神宮: palaces on the map.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　宮（みや）です。
宮（みや）が　すきです。

詩.etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 寺 (phonetic シ) — words measured like temple bells: poetry.
詩.mnemonic: Language that keeps temple time — シ. 詩人: the bell-keeper.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　詩（し）です。
これは　詩（うた）です。

昭.etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 召 (phonetic ショウ) — light called forth: shining, luminous.
昭.mnemonic: The kanji of the 昭和 era — ショウ: the sun summoned onto a whole century.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　昭和（しょうわ）です。
昭和（しょうわ）が　すきです。

meanings: counter for guns, tools, leaves or cakes of something
丁.etymology: Pictograph: a nail seen from the side — borrowed for city blocks (丁目) and for the politeness of 丁寧.
丁.mnemonic: One nail pins one block of the city grid — チョウ. 丁寧: work done to the last nail.

lesson_examples.jp: 丁寧（ていねい）に　せつめいする。
これは　丁度（ちょうど）いいです。

帳.etymology: Phono-semantic: cloth (巾) + 長 (phonetic チョウ) — the long hanging register: account book, notebook.
帳.mnemonic: The ledger unrolling like drapery — チョウ. 手帳: the pocket edition.

lesson_examples.jp: 単語帳（たんごちょう）　作（つく）る　のって　意味（いみ）　あると　思（おも）う？
lesson_examples.en: Do you figure there's any reason to make a vocabulary book?

lesson_examples.jp: これは　手帳（てちょう）です。

笛.etymology: Phono-semantic: bamboo (⺮) + 由 (phonetic テキ) — the bored bamboo pipe: a flute, a whistle.
笛.mnemonic: Bamboo with a reason (由) to sing — ふえ. 口笛: the built-in model.

lesson_examples.jp: これは　笛（ふえ）です。
笛（ふえ）が　すきです。

豆.etymology: Pictograph: a stemmed offering vessel — borrowed long ago for the beans it held.
豆.mnemonic: The dish that became its contents — まめ. 豆腐: beans, transfigured.

lesson_examples.jp: 豆（まめ）の　スープを　飲（の）みます。
これは　豆（まめ）です。

羊.etymology: Pictograph: a sheep's head with curling horns — the favored offering, hiding inside 美, 洋, 善.
羊.mnemonic: Horns, ears, muzzle — ひつじ. The quietest component in the beautiful kanji.

lesson_examples.jp: 羊（ひつじ）が　草（くさ）を　食（た）べて　います。
これは　羊（ひつじ）です。

以.etymology: Oracle-bone form shows a person carrying a tool — 'taking (something) as means': by, with, from a given point (以上, 以下).
以.mnemonic: Grab the tool and the boundary line moves with it — イ. Set the marker: 三つ以上, everything from three up; 以外, everything the tool didn't touch.

lesson_examples.jp: もう　これ　以上（いじょう）　待（ま）てません。
もう　これ　以上（いじょう）　待（ま）てないよ。

英.etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 央 'center' (phonetic エイ) — the central blossom, the finest flower: outstanding; chosen to transcribe 'England' (英国).
英.mnemonic: The one flower standing dead-center of the field, taller than the rest — エイ. It lent its brilliance to a whole language: 英語.

lesson_examples.jp: 母（はは）は　英語（えいご）が　あまり　できません。
